<meta>This page continues the technical explanation of how the "Kabbalistic Art" is applied to the interpretation of sacred texts, moving from the history of its transmission to the specific linguistic methods—transposition, numerical substitution, and ciphers—used to uncover hidden meanings in the Hebrew Bible.</meta>

# BOOK THREE

The whole business is allegorical, where one thing is understood for another, or through another, so that the meaning itself is exchanged for a different one. We shall state clearly that either a word is substituted for a word, or a letter for a word, or a letter for a letter. First, certainly, a word is taken for another word, either through transposition—which is called *metathesis* <note>The rearranging of letters in a word to form a new word.</note>—or through an equal numerical value contained within the words. <note>This refers to Gematria, the practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew letters to find connections between words.</note> A letter is placed for a word either at the beginning, at the end, or anywhere else by means of a mark placed above it. <note>This refers to Notarikon, using letters as acronyms or shorthand.</note> A letter is substituted for a letter through an alphabetic revolution; clearly all of this is done so that every proportion may finally be completed: Arithmetic, Geometric, and Musical. For example, regarding that verse in Psalm 21: "Lord, in your strength the king shall rejoice," <note>original Latin: "Domine in uirtute tua lætabitur rex"</note> we understand this Kabbalistically as referring to the Messiah, saying: "Lord Tetragrammaton, <note>The four-letter divine name (YHWH).</note> in your strength the Messiah King (you may understand) comes or works." For the Messiah is the power of God, and he works in the power of the Tetragrammaton. I am led to this by the word *yismach*, <note>original Hebrew: ישמח, meaning "he shall rejoice."</note> for if its letters are transposed, it becomes *Mashiach*, <note>original Hebrew: משיח</note> that is, the Messiah. Likewise, in another place, the Lord said to Moses: "Because my angel shall go before you" (Exodus 23). Who is that angel according to the Kabbalists? Some say it is Michael, for by transposing the letters of *malakhi*, <note>original Hebrew: מלאכי, meaning "my angel."</note> it becomes Michael. <note>original Hebrew: מיכאל</note> Others, accepting this according to the method of the Kabbalistic art, affirm that it is Metatron, <note>An important angel in Jewish mysticism often associated with the divine presence.</note> because God said, "for my name is in him." In the name Metatron, however, is the name *Shaddai* <note>Meaning "Almighty"; both names share the numerical value of 314.</note> through the equal number contained in both words, a point which Nachmanides <note>original Latin: "Gerundensis," referring to the 13th-century scholar Moses ben Nahman of Girona.</note> wonderfully embraces in the place cited before. Do you now see two symbolic paths of the Kabbalah? Or do you also wish to see the third—a letter replaced for a word? Read Isaiah, chapter 65: "He shall be blessed in the God, Amen." Who is this God? The Kabbalists will answer that it is "Lord, King, Faithful One," <note>original Hebrew: אל ני מלך נאמן (El Adonai Melekh Ne'eman).</note> for the three letters of *Amen* <note>original Hebrew: אמן</note> will mark these three words by their initials, as Recanati <note>original Latin: "Racanat," referring to the 14th-century Italian Kabbalist Menahem Recanati.</note> wrote on Exodus 15. The fourth species and the third part of Kabbalah is literary commutation <note>Known as Temurah, or letter substitution.</note>, so that a word written with certain letters symbolically designates another word composed of different letters. This is done through an alphabetic revolution according to Abraham’s *Book of Creation* <note>original Latin: "librum creationis Abrahæ," referring to the Sefer Yetzirah.</note> with twenty-two variations, according to the fact that as many alphabets are read there. An example is offered to us by *Mazpaz*, <note>original Hebrew: מצפץ</note> a name of God, which is written with these four letters: *mem, tzade, pe, and tzade*. Concerning this, your Pico della Mirandola <note>original Latin: "Mirandulanus uester."</note> says: "The name of God of four letters, which consists of *mem, tzade, pe, and tzade*, ought to be appropriated to the kingdom of David." Since that name is clearly not read in the text of Holy Scripture, what then, I ask, is it held to be a symbol of? The Kabbalists answer that it is a symbol and seal of the ineffable Tetragrammaton, and it proceeds from the last alphabet—which is the twenty-second of the book named *Sefer Yetzirah* and is called *Atbash*. <note>A cipher where the first letter of the alphabet is replaced by the last, the second by the second-to-last, etc.</note> For there, *yod* is exchanged for *mem*, *he* for *tzade*, and *vaw* for *pe*, so that *Mazpaz* is the Lord—*Yod, He, Vaw, He*.

### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART

I have just spoken of those things pertaining to the **art**, which is performed either by crossing, transposing, or commuting words, syllables, or letters, according to four methods <note>original Latin: "quatuor rationes"</note> by which the meanings of the scriptures are ingeniously and skillfully allegorized. For concerning those things that stand without formal art, being made by tradition alone—which I call *Atechna* <note>From the Greek "atechnos," meaning "without art" or "unskilled," referring here to knowledge received directly through tradition rather than through the application of technical rules.</note>—I have made you more than sufficiently certain. Indeed, both of you, through your own professional studies, have already acquired no small amount of knowledge about them: namely, how simple things are abstracted from the composite, and higher things from the lower, so that nearly everything is referred back to the intelligible world, or to the super-supreme and incomparable world.

Moreover, while reading the Holy Scriptures, several arguments for piety may often come to our minds which first entice us toward an admiration of divine things, and then even into a love for them. Yet these cannot be handed down by any certain "art." For example, the idea that the angel **Gabriel** is of stronger virtue than **Michael**, because it is read of him in the Book of **Daniel**: "Twice the power, flying in flight." <note>original Latin: "Duplex uirtus uolando uolans." This refers to Daniel 9:21.</note> Of Michael, however, it is only said that he "comes to help." Therefore, among the Intelligences, Gabriel is philosophically regarded as the power of the **Active Intellect**, and Michael as the power of the **Passible Intellect**. <note>The "Active" and "Passible" (or Passive) Intellects are concepts from Aristotelian philosophy, used here to categorize the celestial hierarchy of angels.</note> So writes **Rabbi Levi Ben Gersom**, who is called by the Latins **Master Leo of Bagnols**.

"It seems to me, most excellent Simon," said **Philolaus**, "to contribute greatly to the Kabbalistic art—even that which you call 'artless.' For unless we have in our hands the revelations of the ancestors (which you rightly think do not fall under the rules of art), then every license for interpreting and turning the Holy Scripture in whatever direction one wished would be granted to everyone, however reckless. This is exactly how we have heard certain common **Sophists** <note>A derogatory term for the Scholastic theologians of the medieval universities, whom the humanists often accused of empty logic-chopping.</note> behave, who in this age seem, with their syllogisms, to have brought those most holy oracles of the Divine Spirit into almost public contempt. But now, when all things are applied to the revelations—as I believe they should be—a certain line is drawn, beyond which the truth cannot stand; thus, the works of the art do not decline into the idleness of the worst of men."

Then Simon said: "You speak the truth openly. For there is almost nothing else that is more erringly twisted to fit any man's personal sense than the divine oracles. Though this is not always due to malice, it is often more due to ignorance. For who would commit a sacrilege against the sacred texts on purpose?

<margin>c</margin> Thus **Saul** was once deceived by the ambiguity of a word and strayed from the oracle. For God had promised in **Exodus 17**: 'I will blot out the memory of Amalek.' <note>original Hebrew: אֶמְחֶה אֶת זֵכֶר עֲמָלֵק (*Emcheh et zeker Amalek*).</note> Saul believed that if he killed the males, the commandment would be satisfied, because the word *zeker* could signify 'male.' <note>original Hebrew: זָכָר (*zakar*).</note> But God intended rather for the 'memory' of Amalek to be destroyed through this word *zeker*, which also designates 'remembrance.' At that time, there was not yet a distinction in the scripture by means of **vowel points and accents**, which only began in the years of **Ezra**. Therefore, the word *Z-K-R* <note>The Hebrew root זכר consists of three consonants; without vowel markings, it can be read as either "memory" or "male."</note>—being written without points and expressing both 'memory' and 'male'—gave Saul the occasion for his ruin."

So spoke Marranus. It happened to both the Italians and the Greeks similarly regarding the word *phos* <note>original: "φως"</note>, which signifies both "man" and "light." Because of this, the ancient worshippers of the Saturnalia were once deceived by the ambiguity of the word <term>amphibologia|The use of ambiguous language or a pun that can be interpreted in two ways.</term> and sacrificed a human being to Saturn every year; yet, according to the oracle, that sacrifice could have just as well been performed by lighting lamps <note>original: "accensis luminibus"</note> to appease Saturn. "The opinion of the more skillful experts, as we have said, is that this Art consists of three things. First, by the calculation of numbers, which is called **Gematria** <note>original: גימטריא</note>, that is, 'Geometry.' By this, a numerical dimension of earthly characters is compared; however, this depends on that higher arithmetic which, due to its abstract simplicity, is not graspable by any of the senses and is therefore not subject to the crude skills of even a novice. Thus, the first part was called 'Geometry' rather than 'Arithmetic,' although in truth both have one and the same value in this art. Second, syllables are sometimes transposed so that the word itself is changed, or the word is simply converted. This second method is when a letter is placed to represent a whole word, and it is called **Notariakon** <note>original: נוטריקון</note> from the shorthand marks of notaries, because there every letter is marked at its peak to serve as a sign for some complete word. Because of this, **Rabbi Joseph the Minor of Salem** <note>Reference to Joseph Gikatilla (1248–1305), a famous Spanish Kabbalist.</note> named the books he wrote on this art 'The Garden' <note>original: גינת - Ginat</note>, because of the three letters of this word, each of which designates one of the three portions of the Kabbalistic art. The *Gimel* [ג] signifies **Gematria** [גימטריא]; the *Nun* [נ] signifies **Notariakon** [נוטריקון]; and the *Tav* [ת] signifies **Temurah** [תמורה]. Thus, these are the parts of the whole craft: **Gematria**, that is, Arithmetic; **Notariakon**, that is, the 'Notary-art' or shorthand; and **Temurah**, that is, the Commutation of elements. To this title, the author alludes to the verse of **Solomon** in the sixth chapter of the **Song of Songs**: 'I went down into the garden of nuts.' <note>Song of Solomon 6:11. In Kabbalah, the 'nut' often symbolizes the layers of mystery surrounding the divine.</note>

For the first part, therefore, I shall begin with that which is the Principle. It is written in **Zechariah** that the Lord of the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God (YHWH), often translated as 'The Lord.'</note> will be *Echad* <note>original: אחד</note>, that is, **One**, and His name *Echad* <note>original: אחד</note>, that is, **One**. Perhaps it is much more true to say the Lord God will be *Aleph* [א], that is, the Beginning—as you say in Greek, 'Alpha and O'—and *Chedo* <note>original: חדו</note>, that is, **One**, as He who is the principle of the One. For He Himself is above all unity, and is the eternal origin of all unity. And perhaps He is not called 'One' just as He is not called 'Being,' because He is above all being from which whatever exists emanates. Whence He is named by the most contemplative ones *Ayin* <note>original: אין</note>, that is, **Non-being** or **Nothingness**, as is read in **Exodus 17**: 'Is the Lord among us as Being, or as Non-being?' <note>Exodus 17:7. The Hebrew 'im ayin' (or not) is interpreted here mystically to mean 'Non-being' (the infinite source beyond existence).</note> It is read, moreover, in the book *On the Way of Faith and Expiation*, that He is both."

<margin>A simple [explanation] of the Kabbalistic Art and its methods</margin>

It is the opinion of the most skilled men, as we have said, that this Art consists of three things. Thus, these are the parts of the whole craft: **Gematria**, which is Arithmetic; **Notarikon**, which is like a notary’s shorthand; and **Temurah**, which is the Commutation of elements. Regarding this title, the author cites the verse of Solomon from the sixth chapter of the Song of Songs:
> "I went down into the garden of nuts." <note>Song of Solomon 6:11. In Kabbalah, the "nut" is often a metaphor for the shell (the literal meaning) hiding the kernel (the mystical meaning).</note>

Therefore, for the first part, I shall begin with that which is the Principle. It is written in Zechariah that the Lord of the Four-Lettered Name <note>The Tetragrammaton, the holy four-letter name of God.</note> shall be **One** <note>original Hebrew: אחד (*Achad*)</note> and His name **One** <note>Hebrew: אחד</note>. Perhaps more truly, the Lord God will be **Aleph** <note>The first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, which is the "Principle" or Beginning—just as you say in Greek, the Alpha and the Omega—and **One**, as He who is the principle of unity. For He is above all unity and is the everlasting origin of all unity. For this reason, He is named by the most contemplative seekers as **Nothingness** <note>original Hebrew: אין (*Ayin*), meaning "Nothing" or "Non-existence." **"Is the Lord among us or is He Nothingness?"** <note>original: "Num est ens Adonai inter nos an nō ens?" Reuchlin translates the Hebrew *Ayin* (meaning "or not") as a noun, "Nothingness," implying a choice between God as a present Being or as the transcendent Nothing.</note>
However, it is read in the book *The Way of Faith and Atonement* that He is both.

# ON THE KABBALISTIC ART

**Being and non-being** <note>original Hebrew: הן ואי (*Hen ve-Ai*); original Latin: *Ens & non ens*</note>, for those things which exist and those which do not exist are from Him and exist after Him. In this way, He is not even "One," because He is the cause of all unity, and unity exists only after Him; nothing among those things that come after Him exists in the same way He does, nor do those things that do not exist. As it says in the *Book of Speculation* <note>The *Sefer ha-Iyun*, a 13th-century Kabbalistic text attributed to the fictional Rabbi Hamai.</note> by **Rabbi Hamai**, who after many words says: **"All things are emanated from His unity, but He is not like any other."** <note>original Hebrew: שכלם נאצלים מאחדותו והוא אינו דומה לאחר (*She-kulam ne’atzalim me-achduto ve-hu eino domeh le-acher*)</note>. 

And it is not only our people who confess this, but your own **Marranus** <note>Referring to one of the speakers in the dialogue, but also nodding to the "Marranos" or New Christians of the era.</note> asserts it as well, whom you prove to be the wisest. For **Dionysius the Areopagite** <note>A 5th-6th century Christian theologian and philosopher whose works were highly influential in medieval mysticism.</note>, in his book *On Mystical Theology*, subscribed to this same opinion regarding God with these words: **"He is neither number, nor order, nor one, nor unity."** <note>original Greek: οὔτε ἀριθμός ἐστιν οὔτε τάξις, οὔτε ἕν, οὔτε ἑνότης (*oute arithmos estin oute taxis, oute hen, oute henotēs*)</note>. 

<margin>C</margin> What then is He? **Simonides** <note>A Greek lyric poet.</note> answered **Hiero**: "The more I think about it, the less I understand." The same thing happens to me; when I have passed beyond all created things and ascended above all **being** <note>original Latin: *ens*</note>, I find nothing other than an infinite sea of nothingness, and the fountain of all being flowing perpetually from the abyss of darkness. Oh, the height! Oh, the depth! Oh, our weakness! 

But it ought to seem sufficient to us to know of Him that which He has revealed to us about Himself: that He is this **Beginning** <note>The letter Aleph (א), the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.</note>, which is **Aleph**, and the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, יהוה (YHWH), often rendered as "the LORD."</note> which is signified by Aleph. It denotes the divine essence, which is nothing other than **YHWH** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה</note>; this is almost the same as **Essence** <note>original Latin: *essentia*</note>. 

<margin>E</margin> For because of their equal numerical value, Scripture joined them together as the one who is the first and the last, as in Exodus 9: **"Behold, the hand of the Tetragrammaton is 'being'"** <note>original Hebrew: הנה יד יהוה הויה (*Hineh yad YHWH hoyah*). Reuchlin is playing on the word *hoyah* (is/being), which has the same numerical value as the Name.</note>. This "being" is, as it were, the end of the works and miracles of God, as is clear in the ten plagues of Egypt. Indeed, that expression is not found elsewhere in this way. 

<margin>F</margin> Furthermore, by the testimony of **Solomon of Troyes** <note>Known as Rashi (1040–1105), the preeminent medieval French rabbi and commentator.</note>, it indicates a present essence. Because the Tetragrammaton begins with the letter **Yod**, it was clearly done for our sake, so that we might recognize that He is the infinite point and the fulfillment of every number—that is, of every created thing. For **Yod** signifies **ten**. 

And in the expansion <note>A kabbalistic technique of "spelling out" a name to find hidden meanings or numerical values.</note> of the name Tetragrammaton, the tenth letter is repeated thus: **YHWH YHW YHY** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה יהו יהי</note>. Where, after the Tetragrammaton, **YHY** is repeated, which is the symbol of **Ehieh** <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (*Ehyeh*), meaning "I Am."</note> itself; that is, it signifies "Being" through the equality of its number. 

And it signifies no less the essence of the Creator, as in Exodus 3: **"I AM [Ehieh] has sent me to you."** Not that essence which remains within, but that which flows outward. For the seal of God is **YHWH**, which **Ehieh** sealed the world with, and it is called **Truth** <note>original Hebrew: אמת (*Emet*)</note>, because it is born from multiplying itself arithmetically. 

Then follows **Yah** <note>original Hebrew: יה</note>, the name of the essence of merit and retribution, as in the Psalms: "If you, **Yah**, should mark iniquities." Therefore, you see three essential names in the Tetragrammaton. The **Ineffable** Name denotes the primary essence; **Ehieh** denotes essence in things; and **Yah** denotes essence in merits; and they are predicated on "what" a thing is. And that is called **Mah** <note>original Hebrew: מה (*Mah*), meaning "What."</note>. For the Tetragrammaton spelled out—**Yod He Vav He** <note>original Hebrew: יוד הא ואו הא</note>—signifies **Mah** through the equality of number; for both contain the value of **forty-five**. 

And when Moses said, "What is His name? What shall I say?" the answer given to him was **"Ehieh."** Then, consider diligently the words of the Holy Spirit which...

### BOOK THREE.

...words which are not placed in vain in that same passage of Exodus 3: <term>What is his name? What?</term> <note>original Hebrew: מה שמו מה (*Mah shemo mah*). Reuchlin is highlighting a Kabbalistic method where the final letters of these words—He, Vav, and He—reveal a version of the Divine Name.</note> That is: "To me, what is his name? What?" And look at their terminal letters, and you will have that ineffable three-letter name <term>YHV</term> <note>original Hebrew: יהו (*Yud-He-Vav*)</note>, the beginning of which is <term>I shall be</term> <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (*Ehieh*)</note>. The middle is <term>Iah</term> <note>original Hebrew: יה (*Yah*)</note>. The end is infinity. For its parts are <term>YH</term>, <term>HV</term>, and <term>VY</term> <note>original Hebrew: יה הו וי</note>, which we shall divide into three intervals. The first is <term>YH</term>, the second is <term>HV</term>, the third is <term>VY</term>. All of these serve "to be" and "essence." Regarding <term>Iah</term>, we read in Exodus 15: *My strength and my praise is Iah*. Regarding <term>YHV</term> in the same place: *And he has become my salvation*. Regarding <term>YHV</term> in the first chapter of Genesis: *Let there be light*. These two newest words contributed very much to the crafting of the world and the existence of things, as in: <term>Let there be light, and there was light</term> <note>original Hebrew: יהי אור ויהי אור (*Yehi or va-yehi or*). Reuchlin notes that the Hebrew word for "let there be" (*Yehi*) uses the letters of the Divine Name.</note>. *And there was evening, and there was morning. Let there be a firmament, and let there be a distinction, and it was so. Let the waters be gathered, and it was so. Let the earth sprout, and it was so. Let the earth bring forth, and it was so. Let there be lights, and it was so.* Always adding that: *and there was evening and there was morning.* In all these things, so that they may truly exist, we discover that the ineffable name is present seminally and hiddenly. 

Indeed, we see only <term>Elohim</term> (that is, God) expressed in those six days. But when the world already appeared to be perfect, after the various and wonderful works of the most divine powers were finished, and at last a deserved triumph was to be celebrated and a feast day declared—behold, with <term>Elohim</term>, the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH, which Jews do not pronounce aloud. Reuchlin uses the Latinized "Tetragrammatus" here.</note>, King of kings and Lord of lords, entered. And then for the first time it was said: *These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created in the day that the Tetragrammaton Elohim made the heaven and the earth.* Here the Tetragrammaton first thundered publicly to the ears of all creatures, by which we understand the mercy of God joined with justice. For in whatever place of Holy Scripture the Tetragrammaton joins <term>Elohim</term> to itself, there we notice the property of mercy and justice together. 

Sometimes it is composed with <term>Iah</term>, as in the prayer of Habakkuk: *The Tetragrammaton Adonai is my strength.* And we, by reading it thus, understand the power of the Tetragrammaton to descend to the spoken name <term>Adonai</term> <note>Adonai means "Lord" and is the word usually spoken aloud when the Tetragrammaton (YHWH) appears in text.</note> itself. If, however, it is found in reverse order, <term>Adonai Tetragrammaton</term>, as in Genesis 15: *Adonai Tetragrammaton, what will you give me?* then we conceive in the mind that the <term>numerations</term> <note>original Latin: *numerationes*. This refers to the *Sefirot*, the ten attributes or "emanations" of God in Kabbalah.</note>—that is, the divine properties—ascending from the lower to the higher, reach the supreme light. 

It also happens sometimes that the name <term>El</term> <note>A common Semitic word for "God" or "Might."</note> is found joined to it, as in Psalm 118: *The El Tetragrammaton has shone upon us*, and it signifies mercy. Not dissimilarly when <term>Elohim</term> is added and it is said thus: *The El Elohim Tetragrammaton has spoken and called the earth* (in Psalm 50); then it denotes the ineffable name clothed in grace and severity. Sometimes it is read—and only in the Prophets and the Hagiographa <note>The *Ketuvim* or "Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible.</note>—as <term>Tetragrammaton Sabbaoth</term> <note>Sabbaoth means "of Hosts" or "of Armies."</note>. In Psalm 46: *The Tetragrammaton Sabbaoth is with us, our protector is the God of Jacob.* This way, it suggests the property of judgment. And therefore the Prophets use this manner of address when rebuking with severity.

# ON THE ART OF THE KABBALAH

->He is and He is not<- <note>original Hebrew: הוא ואין (*Hu ve-ayin*)</note>, that is: <term>Being & non-being</term>. For those things which exist, and those which do not exist, are from Him and are after Him. In this way, He is also "not one," because He is the cause of all unity, and unity exists only after Him. Nothing that exists after Him is quite like Him, just as nothing that does not exist is like Him. This is found in the *Book of Speculation* by <term>Rabbi Hamai</term>, who says after many other points: <note>original Hebrew: שכלם נאצלים מאחדותו והוא אינו דומה לאחר (*She-kulam ne’etzalim me-achduto ve-hu eino domeh le-acher*)</note>. This means: "That all things derive from His unity, and He Himself is not similar to that unity."

Nor is it only our people who admit this; even your own <term>Marranes</term> <note>Reuchlin likely means "sages" or "teachers" here, though the term often referred to converted Jews; in this context, he is referring to Christian authorities</note>, whom you prove to be most wise, assert the same. For <term>Dionysius the Areopagite</term>, in his book *On Mystical Theology*, subscribed to this same sentiment regarding God with these words: <note>original Greek: οὔτε ἀριθμός ἐστιν οὔτε τάξις; οὔτε ἕν, οὔτε ἑνότης (*oute arithmos estin oute taxis; oute hen, oute henotes*)</note>. That is: <margin>C</margin> "God is neither number, nor order, nor the one, nor unity."

What then is He? <term>Simonides</term> answered <term>Hiero</term>: "The more I think about it, the less I understand." The same thing happens to me: when I have moved past all created things and ascended above all being, I find nothing other than an infinite sea of "nothingness," and the fountain of all entity flowing eternally from the abyss of darkness. Oh height! Oh depth! Oh our own weakness!

Yet it ought to seem sufficient to us to know of Him that which He has revealed of Himself to us. Because He is the Beginning—that is <term>Aleph</term>—and the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> which is signified by the letter Aleph. It denotes the divine essence, which is certainly nothing other than <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (*Ehieh*)</note>, namely "I shall be." This is almost the same as the essence of <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (*YHVH*)</note>. <margin>E</margin> For because of their equal value, Scripture joined both together as belonging to Him who is the first and the last. In Exodus 9: <note>original Hebrew: הנה יד יהוה הויה (*Hineh yad Adonai hoyah*)</note>. That is: <margin>F</margin> "Behold, the hand of the Tetragrammaton is becoming," <note>Reuchlin interprets the Hebrew *hoyah* ("is" or "is present") as a form of the Divine Name related to "being."</note> as if to say, this is the end of the works and miracles of God, as is clear in the ten plagues of Egypt. For elsewhere that expression is not found in this way. Moreover, the testimony of <term>Solomon of Troyes</term> <note>Referring to the famous commentator Rashi</note> indicates a present essence.

As for the fact that the Tetragrammaton begins with the letter <term>Yod</term>, this was clearly done for our sake, so that we might recognize that He Himself is the infinite point, and the fulfillment of every number—that is, of every thing. For the letter Yod signifies ten. And in the expansion of the name Tetragrammaton, the tenth letter is as follows: <note>original Hebrew: יהוה יהו יהי (*YHVH, YHV, YHI*)</note>. Where, after the Tetragrammaton, <note>original Hebrew: יהי (*YHI*)</note> is repeated, which is the symbol of *Ehieh* itself; that is, of "Being," by an equality of number. <note>Through the method of Gematria, where letters have numerical values, Reuchlin argues that *YHI* ("Let there be") and *Ehieh* ("I shall be") share a mystical equivalence.</note>

And it nonetheless signifies the essence of the Creator, as in Exodus 3: "I shall be [Ehieh] has sent me to you," not that essence which remains within, but that which flows outward. For the seal of God is <note>original Hebrew: אמת (*Emet*)</note>, "Truth," with which *Ehieh* sealed the world. And it is called <note>original Hebrew: אמת (*Emet*)</note>—that is, "True"—precisely because it is born from multiplying itself arithmetically. Then follows <note>original Hebrew: יה (*Iah*)</note>, the name of the essence of merit and retribution, as in the Psalms: "If you, Iah, should mark iniquities."

Therefore, you see three essential names in the Tetragrammaton. The Ineffable Name denotes the first essence. <term>Ehieh</term> denotes the essence in things. And <term>Iah</term> denotes the essence in merits. They are predicated on "what" He is. And that is called <note>original Hebrew: מה (*Mah*)</note>, that is: "What." For the Tetragrammaton, when spelled out as <note>original Hebrew: יוד הא ואו הא (*Yud-He-Vav-He*)</note>, signifies "What" [Mah] through equality of number; for both contain the value of forty-five. <note>This is the "Name of 45." The letters of YHVH spelled out—Yud (10,6,4), He (5,1), Vav (6,1,6), He (5,1)—total 45. The Hebrew word *Mah* (Mem=40, He=5) also totals 45.</note> And when Moses said: "What is His name? What shall I say?" He answered him, "I shall be" [Ehieh]. Then, consider diligently the work of the Holy Spirit...

### BOOK THREE.

...words which are not placed in vain in that same passage of Exodus 3: <note>original Hebrew: מה שמו מה (*Mah shemo mah*)</note>. That is: "What is His name, what?" And look at their terminal letters; you will have there that ineffable three-lettered name <note>original Hebrew: יהוה (*YHVH* - though the text mentions terminal letters of the previous phrase, which are H, V, H, it links them to the four-lettered name)</note> whose beginning is *Ehieh* <note>meaning "I Shall Be"</note>. The middle is *Iah*. The end is infinity. For its parts are <note>original Hebrew: יה יה יה (*Yah, Yah, Yah*)</note>, which we divide into three intervals. The first is *Yah*, the second is *Yah*, the third is *Yah*. All of these serve "to be" and "essence." Regarding *Iah*, we read in Exodus 15: "My strength and my praise is *Jah*." Regarding the Tetragrammaton in that same place: "And He has become my salvation." Regarding the Tetragrammaton in the first chapter of Genesis: "Let there be light." These two most recent words contributed greatly to the craftsmanship of the world and the existence of things, as in: <note>original Hebrew: יהי אור ויהי אור (*Yehi or va-yehi or*)</note>, "Let there be light, and there was light." There was evening, and there was morning; "Let there be a firmament," and "let there be a division," and "it was done so." "Let the waters be gathered," and "it was done so." "Let the earth bring forth," and "it was done so." "Let the earth produce," and "it was done so." "Let there be lights," and "it was done so." Always with this added: "and there was evening and there was morning." In all these things, so that they may truly exist, we perceive the ineffable name to be present seminally and hiddenly. 

However, we see only *Elohim* <note>The Hebrew name for God associated with power and judgment</note>, that is, God, expressed during those six days. But when the world appeared to be perfected, after the various and wonderful works of the most divine powers were completed, and finally a well-deserved triumph was to be celebrated and a feast day proclaimed, behold—the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-lettered name YHVH, often associated with Mercy</note> stepped forth with *Elohim* as the King of kings and Lord of lords. Then it was said for the first time: "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, in the day that the <term>Tetragrammaton-Elohim</term> <note>The combined name YHVH-Elohim</note> made the heaven and the earth." Here the Tetragrammaton first thundered publicly in the ears of all creatures, by which we understand the mercy of God joined with His justice. For in whatever place of Holy Scripture the Tetragrammaton joins itself to *Elohim*, there we observe the property of mercy and justice together. 

It is sometimes composed with <note>original Hebrew: אדני (*Adonai*)</note>, as in the prayer of Habakkuk: "The Tetragrammaton <term>Adonai</term> <note>Lord</note> is my strength." By reading it thus, we understand the power of the Tetragrammaton to descend to *Adonai* itself as it is spoken. If, however, it is found in the reverse order, *Adonai*-Tetragrammaton, as in Genesis 15: "Lord <note>Adonai</note> Tetragrammaton, what will you give me?" then we conceive in the mind through the <term>numerations</term> <note>The Sefirot, or divine emanations</note>—that is, the divine properties—ascending from the lower to the higher, that they may take hold of the supreme light. 

It also happens sometimes that the name *El* is found joined to it, as in Psalm 118: "*El* <note>God/The Mighty One</note> the Tetragrammaton has shone upon us," and this signifies mercy. It is not dissimilar when *Elohim* is added and it is said: "*El Elohim* the Tetragrammaton has spoken and called the earth," in the fiftieth Psalm; then the ineffable name denotes grace clothed in severity. Sometimes it is read—and this only in the Prophets and the <term>Hagiographa</term> <note>The "Holy Writings," the third section of the Hebrew Bible</note>—as "Tetragrammaton <term>Sabbaoth</term>" <note>Lord of Hosts</note>. In Psalm 46: "The Tetragrammaton *Sabbaoth* is with us, the God of Jacob is our protector." In this way, it suggests the property of judgment. And for that reason, the Prophets use that style when rebuking, for the purpose of severity.

<meta>This page continues the discussion from page 74 regarding the mystical properties of the Tetragrammaton (the four-letter name of God, YHWH). Reuchlin is now moving into the specific derivations of other divine names—like El, Eloha, and Elohim—from the core name, using both grammatical and numerological (Gematria) methods common in Kabbalistic study.</meta>

<header>ON THE CABALISTIC ART</header>

You will be able to search more extensively for explanations of this kind in the book *Gates of Light*, and most extensively of all in the book *Gates of Justice* by Rabbi Joseph Gikatilla <note>original: "Ioseph Carnitolis." Joseph Gikatilla (1248–c. 1305) was a Spanish Kabbalist. Reuchlin’s "Carnitolis" is a corruption of Gikatilla's name.</note>. Furthermore, concerning the thirteen properties of that same Tetragrammaton, which the Law-giver Moses invoked in Exodus 34, according to this sense:

> O Tetragrammaton <note>Reuchlin uses the vocative "Tetragrammate" to address God by his four-letter name.</note>, Lord God, merciful and gracious, patient, of great compassion, and true; keeping mercy unto the thousands, taking away iniquity, passing over crime and sin; and the innocent He will not treat as innocent, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children into the third and fourth generation.

I call upon you here, O most excellent men—for it is permitted to say this surely and without falsehood—since much labor and many words would be needed by anyone who wished to make public all the mysteries of the name Tetragrammaton, of which no end is ever found, just as there is no end to the substance of God. Therefore, leaving aside the proper name of the divine essence, I shall show a few of its derivatives. For it is customary, according to the decree of the grammarians, that we form common names from proper ones. These are **God**, **God**, and **God** <note>original Hebrew: אֵל (*El*), אֱלוֹהַּ (*Eloha*), and אֱלֹהִים (*Elohim*). Reuchlin is translating all three as versions of "God."</note>, each of which has obtained its origin from the ineffable Tetragrammaton. That name contains four letters—look, four—and designates the number twenty-six <note>In Gematria, the numerical value of Y-H-V-H (10+5+6+5) is 26.</note>—look, twenty-six—all of which are a single symbol of God—look, one. Join these individuals together, namely four, twenty-six, and one, and it becomes **These** <note>original Hebrew: אֵלֶּה (*Elle*, meaning "these"). Numerically: Aleph(1) + Lamed(30) + He(5) = 36. However, Reuchlin's math (4+26+1) equals 31, which is the value of **El** (אֵל: Aleph=1, Lamed=30).</note>. If you add the termination of the Tetragrammaton, **H** <note>the letter ה (*He*)</note>, then *Eloha* is born. 

Now concerning *Elohim*, it is said that its "Mem" <note>the final letter 'm'</note> is not a part of the word's meaning, but a grammatical inflection, as is apparent from this: if it must be read through a suffix or a grammatical construction, there is no doubt it will lack the letter Mem. Therefore, if you add **God** <note>original: *El*</note> to the beginning of the Tetragrammaton **Iah** in reverse order, it soon becomes *Elohi*, and by assuming the grammatical declension, which is Mem, it will be pronounced *Elohim* at the end. This is often written with the letters of the Ineffable Name, yet it is nonetheless pointed <note>provided with vowel marks</note> as *Elohim*. 

In the Cabala, there is a frequent use of reversed order, and great is its power and the praise of its power; for in whatever way the syllables are transposed, the letters remain the same without loss, though often the meanings are not the same. Abraham mentions this matter in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *Liber Ietzira* (Sefer Yetzirah), an ancient foundational text of Jewish mysticism.</note> when he says: **Male and female, male in Emes and female in Esem** <note>original Hebrew: זכר ונקבה זכר באמש ונקבה באמש (*Zachar u-nekevah zachar be-emesh u-nekevah be-ashem*). Reuchlin is showing how transposing the letters of *Emesh* (Aleph-Mem-Shin) into *Ashem* (Aleph-Shin-Mem) changes the concept from male to female.</note>. Here the transposition of letters indicates a change in the thing itself. For example, **No** and **God** <note>original Hebrew: לֹא (*Lo*, "no") and אֵל (*El*, "God"). They consist of the same two letters, Lamed and Aleph, in different orders.</note>. 

While this is common in other cases, it is profoundly admirable in this Ineffable Name: no matter how much its letters are turned this way and that, they always signify one and the same thing—namely, the Being and Essence of God, who said:

> I am the Tetragrammaton, and I do not change. <note>A reference to Malachi 3:6: "I am the Lord (YHWH), I change not."</note>

This will be made more manifest to you by this practice: let the name Tetragrammaton be resolved into twelve variations (for we cannot proceed beyond that); then, whatever shall be found...

<meta>This page continues the discussion of the various names of God. Having just introduced the common names of God (El, Eloha, Elohim), Reuchlin now transitions into the permutations of the four-letter name (Tetragrammaton) and the mystical relationships between the names Adonai, Elohim, and Shaddai.</meta>

## BOOK THREE

...if it occurs, it will serve none other than the Essence, whose symbols are these: **YHWH, YHWH, YHWH** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה יהוה יהוה</note>. These twelve names are therefore considered by the <term>Cabalists: Practitioners of Kabbalah, a school of Jewish mysticism that seeks to understand the relationship between the eternal, mysterious Infinite and the mortal, finite universe.</term> as one single name, as if signifying one single thing, even though there are twelve explanations. To each of these explanations, they apply one clause from Holy Scripture that aptly relates to it through <term>Notariacon: A Kabbalistic system of acrostics where the initial or final letters of words in a sentence form a new word.</term>, not for the sake of exposition, but only as a memory aid so that it is not forgotten. 

For instance, if I were to say: "Pay attention and hear, O Israel, today," which is read in Deuteronomy 27 <note>original Latin: "Attende & audi Israel hodie"; Deuteronomy 27:9</note>. In Hebrew this is *Hasket ve-shema Yisrael* <note>original Hebrew: הסכת ושמע ישראל</note>. If you take the first letters of these four words, they make **YHWH** <note>Reuchlin is demonstrating a mnemonic where the first letters of a biblical phrase spell out the divine name.</note>, which is the name of the Essence and the resolution of the Tetragrammaton; let the other names be formed from the others in like manner. 

But let us remain for a little while in this first type of Kabbalah while we look at certain things still necessary to know. For what I have just said should actually have been taken from the second part. Let us, however, approach this art limb by limb and piece by piece, if you will, provided we do not linger too long on each one, so that the day's work passes with the day. Indeed, I will now cite again quite briefly what I touched upon before, so that it may stick more firmly: that God before creation was "Ineffable"; in creation He was named **Elohim**; and after creation, dwelling in the world as if in His own temple, He is called **Adonai** <note>original Hebrew: אדני. Translates to "Lord."</note>. 

Hence we read in Psalm 11: "The Tetragrammaton is in His holy temple, the Tetragrammaton's throne is in the heavens," as one who rules over His own works. For He Himself is, as the Scripture says in Deuteronomy 10: "The God of gods and the Lord of lords, the great God <note>original: "El magnus"</note>." Therefore, the "Temple" is Kabbalistically noted as **Adonai**, and vice versa, through equality of number <note>This refers to Gematria. The Hebrew word for Temple, *Heikhal* (היכל), has a numerical value of 65, which is identical to the value of the name *Adonai* (אדני).</note>. Just as in **Adonai**, as if in His own temple <note>original Hebrew: היכל (*Heikhal*)</note>, the Ineffable Tetragrammaton is to be adored, and God is to be loved in God, according to the triple world, as in Jeremiah 7: "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord." 

There remains another descriptive name, **Shaddai** <note>original Hebrew: שדי</note>, that is, *Sadai*. In Exodus 6 it says: "I am the Tetragrammaton, and I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as **El Shaddai**, but my name Tetragrammaton I did not make known to them." Here, only this is called His "name" which is ineffable, because this alone is proper to the Highest God, insofar as He Himself is nothing of those things that exist, but is above all things, having no regard outside of Himself. 

Other names are descriptive of other properties and relations, such as **Shaddai**, which the Latins have translated as "Omnipotent." However, it is more aptly signified in Hebrew as "Self-sufficient," content in Himself and needing nothing, which the Greeks more correctly interpret as "self-sufficient" <note>original Greek: αὐτάρκης (*autarkēs*)</note>. For we say grammatically that *She* <note>original Hebrew: ש</note> means "who" and *Dai* <note>original Hebrew: די</note> means "is enough" or "is sufficient." Furthermore, if you hear the word "The Name" <note>original: "nomen"</note> used solitarily in the sacred rites, let the Tetragrammaton immediately come to your mind, which is called the Name above every name "by way of excellence" <note>original Greek: κατ’ ἐξοχὴν (*kat’ exochen*)</note> and hyperbolically, however much in daily speech it may refer to any thing that has existence.

-># ON THE CABALISTIC ART<-

**Shaddai** <note>original Hebrew: שדי (*Shaddai*), often translated as "Almighty"</note> however, because he has no need for the assistance of another, appeared to the patriarchs in **El Shaddai**—that is, in the Mighty One who is satisfied in himself. The **Tetragrammaton** <note>The four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> appeared as He who is sufficient in Himself to perform miracles and wonders. However, He did not let them know that the name Tetragrammaton is that name in which a man, acting as a cooperator and delegate of God, can perform miracles; concerning this, I have written more clearly in **Capnion's** <note>Reuchlin's own pen name, derived from the Greek word for "smoke"</note> *On the Miracle-Working Word* <note>original Latin: *De Verbo Mirifico*, Reuchlin’s 1494 work on the power of the divine name</note>. 

Furthermore, there is a ministering spirit belonging to Shaddai himself called **Metattron** <note>Metatron, a high-ranking angel in Jewish mysticism who often serves as a celestial scribe or mediator</note>, so named because of the equality of the number <note>The numerical value (Gematria) of the name Shaddai is 314, which is identical to the value of the name Metatron</note>. He is held to be the leader and the one who shows the way, which we will treat more clearly later if you remind me. 

To this is added another name, **Sabaoth** <note>original Hebrew: צבאות (*Tzevaot*)</note>, which is read thus in Hebrew and signifies "armies" or "hosts." These are described in three ways: 
1. The first is of the entirely separated intelligences and the **angels**. 
2. The second is of the movers of the celestial spheres and the assisting **powers**. 
3. The third is of the **souls** that give form to bodies. 

This name is not found except following the name of God. Thus it is also read in a threefold way: "Holy, Holy, Holy, Tetragrammaton Sabaoth," in the sixth chapter of Isaiah and similarly in other places. 

You have now heard the status of the entire first part of the **Kabbalah** <note>original Latin: *Cabala*</note> and the system by which it proceeds. Since it consists entirely in the permutation of sacred words, and any words can be altered in two ways, we must necessarily admit that there are two species underlying this part: 
1. The **transposition of syllables or words** <term>Temurah: A Kabbalistic method of rearranging letters to find hidden meanings.</term>.
2. The **equality of numbers** <term>Gematria: A system where each Hebrew letter corresponds to a number, allowing words with the same total value to be related to one another.</term>. 

For example, if I read in the fortieth chapter of Isaiah: "Who created these?" <note>original Hebrew: אלה ברא (*Ele Bara*)</note> and I Kabbalistically transpose these two, I might convert them into: "Who created these? God created" <note>original Hebrew: מי אלה ברא אלהים (*Mi Ele bara Elohim*). Reuchlin is showing how the letters of "these created" can be rearranged to reveal the word "Elohim" (God)</note> so that the meaning stands firm. 

And in **Ezekiel**, he sat by the river **Chebar** <note>original Hebrew: כבר (*Kevar*)</note>, that is, at the influence of the **Cherub** <note>original Hebrew: כרוב (*Keruv*)</note>; for if the letters are transposed, "Blessed" <note>original Hebrew: ברוך (*Baruch*)</note> becomes "Cherub." 

And **Noah** found grace <note>Genesis 6:8</note>; by converting the letters, "Grace" <note>original Hebrew: חן (*Chen*)</note> becomes "Noah" <note>original Hebrew: נח (*Noach*)</note>. 

All such things happen through **metathesis** <note>the transposition of sounds or letters in a word</note> because of the primary confusion of letters that had appeared in the **fiery globe** <note>A reference to the Kabbalistic idea that the alphabet existed in a chaotic, primordial state of light before the creation of the world</note>, as if it were permitted to draw the letters out of chaos and read them from one side or the other; thus the first species of the first part is completed.

Now I have decided for myself to show something by way of example from the second branch of this first part, so that you may know the matter more clearly and hold it more firmly in your memory. It is read concerning **Isaac** and **Rebecca** in Genesis 25: "and Rebecca his wife conceived" <note>original Hebrew: ותהר רבקה אשתו (*Vatahar Rivkah Ishto*)</note>. From this, it is granted to us to divine what Rebecca actually conceived. Indeed, as the words indicate, Rebecca conceived "**his wife**" <note>original Hebrew: אשתו (*Ishto*)</note>. 

But you, most learned men, consider what "his wife" <note>original Hebrew: אשתו (*Ishto*)</note> is in this second species of the first part through **Gematria** (that is, the measurement of numbers). You will find that according to the equality of the number, it signifies "**Fire and Stubble**" <note>original Hebrew: אש וקש (*Esh ve-Kash*)</note>. For each contains within itself **seven hundred and seven**. Rebecca therefore conceived fire and stubble, which the sacred words confirm, as witnessed by **Obadiah**, who says: "And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Esau stubble" <note>Obadiah 1:18. Jacob and Esau were the twins in Rebecca's womb</note>. Similarly...

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of Kabbalistic methods by the character Simon. Having previously discussed Gematria (numerical values), he now demonstrates how the word for "Wisdom" contains the number of all divine commandments and transitions into the history of the Hebrew script before introducing the second method: Notariqon.</meta>

### BOOK THREE

When we hear that the Law was given in **Wisdom** <note>original Hebrew: חכמה (*Chochmah*)</note>, let us see what that Wisdom is which is suitable for the enactment of the Law. Certainly, there are edicts and interdicts, commands and prohibitions. However, "Wisdom" is a symbol for all the commandments of God. For when you pronounce the four elements of that word according to their own spellings—**Chet, Kaph, Mem, He** <note>original Hebrew: חית כף מם הי. In the system of *Gematria Millui* (filling out the names of letters), the values are: Chet (חית = 418), Kaph (כף = 100), Mem (מם = 80), and He (הי = 15). Together they sum to 613</note>—there is forged from them the number of the six hundred and thirteen commandments of God, which our teachers call **Taryag** <note>original Hebrew: תריג (*Taryag*). This is a mnemonic where Tav=400, Resh=200, Yod=10, Gimel=3, totaling 613</note>.

In the highest level of this kind of speculation, it will be worthy of mention that, first, the characters, elements, and letters of the Law were stored in a confused mass, readable this way and that. Second, they were not distinguished by any accents or points. Third, each individual primordial letter of the alphabet signified a certain number—even the five terminal letters, which the wise **Ezra** <note>The biblical scribe Ezra, credited by tradition with introducing the "Square" Assyrian script and the vowel system</note> invented along with the points long afterward. For there are twenty-two primitive letters, in which alone all Scripture was depicted from the beginning; to this day, the Kabbalists place and displace them for the delight of whatever pleasant contemplation they wish.

Finally, we must aim for this universal goal: although it is the duty of the Kabbalist to read one thing and understand another, everyone must nevertheless observe this rule as inviolable: apply good to good and evil to evil, lest one apply black to white, or day to night.

Then **Marranus** <note>One of the three interlocutors in Reuchlin's dialogue</note> said: "I would consider that kind of art no differently than if someone called a certain **Dorotheus** by the name **Theodorus**, or **Demonicus** instead of **Nicodemus**, or **Philodemus** for **Demophilus**. Just as the Greeks are accustomed to saying **'lover of the body'** and **'body-loving'**." <note>original Greek: σωματοφίλον καὶ φιλοσώματον. Marranus is suggesting that Kabbalah is merely a system of anagrams or word-play</note>

To these things **Simon** replied: "Certainly, what you say is not entirely off the mark, but you will grow weary very quickly in listing examples because of the poverty of other languages. Compared to Hebrew—which is the fountain of all languages—they are poor and impatient with their own lack, so much so that they adopt the idioms of other nations. They neither accept the full number of letters nor admit a useful composition. Therefore, this art can by no means be translated into the speech of another nation. If I did not know you were equally skilled in Hebrew, I would have discussed these few matters of Kabbalah with you in vain, and would be in vain to continue now."

"But quickly, let us proceed to the second part of this instruction, which is called **Notariqon** <note>original Hebrew: נוטריקון. A method of shorthand or acronyms</note>, that is, the 'notarial' art. This is a certain convention secretly accepted among Kabbalists, where single letters designate certain words without the joining of syllables, just as is the custom for notaries and clerks. Once, in the conduct of war, people brought forth the secrets of the mind through 'stolen' writings using single letters placed in a disorganized way. There is even a commentary by the grammarian **Probus**, as **Aulus Gellius** <note>A 2nd-century Roman author who wrote about the history of shorthand and cryptic writing in his *Attic Nights*</note> writes, which was quite carefully made concerning the hidden meaning of letters. Perhaps something similar happens in the pursuit of this skill, as if people agreed among themselves that the letter **Yod** <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, often associated with a single point</note>, because of its shape as an indivisible point..."

<meta>This page continues the technical exposition of Kabbalistic methods by the character Simon. Having previously discussed Gematria (numerical values), he now transitions into the second method: Notariqon, where individual letters stand for entire words or phrases, using the historical example of Judas Maccabeus and the writing on the wall in Babylon.</meta>

# ON THE KABBALISTIC ART

...noting the unspeakable **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH</note>, which we commonly translate as "Lord." Just as they are also accustomed to mark that very name with three points on account of the three **summits** <note>original Hebrew: עלין (*Alin*); referring to the three points or "prongs" on certain Hebrew letters or the three highest emanations of God</note> in the ten numerations <note>The Sephirot, or divine attributes</note>, which are one and the same **Crown** <note>original Hebrew: עטרת (*Ataret*); usually referring to Keter, the highest Sephirah</note>. For the Kabbalists say: *Because of this mystery they write the Name with three Yods in this way* <note>original Hebrew: כי לסוד זה כותבין השם ג' יודיין בזה</note>, that is, **YYY** <note>original Hebrew: ייי</note>, where the unique four-letter name is written with three single letters, which is approved by daily usage.

And there was once in the days of **Antiochus Eupator** <note>A Seleucid king of the 2nd century BCE</note>, Judas son of Mattathias, a noble warrior and a most fierce leader of war for the laws, the temple, the city, the fatherland, and the citizens of the Jews. When Antiochus and his entire army were rushing against them, Judas, warned by an angel, gave to his comrades-in-arms—as a battle signal—this noble sign: **MKBI** <note>original Hebrew: מכבי (*Maccabee*)</note>, so that they might bravely exhort themselves in battle with these four letters. He promised that it would be a sign of God’s victory, which the Jewish soldiers accepted with joyful hearts as a source of great consolation. Under that standard, fighting valiantly, they slew fourteen thousand men in the camp of Antiochus, along with a huge number of elephants and those who had been placed upon them.

As a result, the leader of the war, Judas, who was previously called by that name, was henceforth nicknamed **Maccabeus** by everyone, because these four characters sounded this way when spoken as syllables. Since they believed themselves to be the victors of so many battles through the power of that sign, the military tribunes and the wise men in Israel marveled, asking Judas in what way so many triumphs had occurred under this sign given to them. Judas Maccabeus responded that in that sign was the presence of the ineffable, Almighty God.

He showed them those words of Moses in **Exodus 15**, saying: *Who is like unto thee among the mighty, O Tetragrammaton?* <note>original Hebrew: מי כמוך באלים יהוה (*Mi Chamocha Ba'elim Hashem*)</note>. For these four characters <note>M-K-B-I</note> designate these words as their initials. In this, the letter **Yod** <note>The 'I' or 'Y' at the end of MKBI</note> is clearly understood to signify the name Tetragrammaton. Indeed, **MKBI** is a memorable symbol for the divine name of seventy-two letters <note>A complex Kabbalistic name of God derived from Exodus</note> through the equality of number. And those of Judas's army, being moved, fought again and prostrated no fewer than thirty-five thousand men, as the writings indicate, being wonderfully delighted by the presence of God and blessing the Almighty Lord Tetragrammaton in their native tongue.

From this, therefore, you understand that an entire word can be signified by a single letter, whether that letter stands alone or whether it completes any other word collectively. Just as a whole phrase is said to note an entire sentence, as in the fifth chapter of **Daniel**: *Numbered, weighed, divided* <note>original Hebrew/Aramaic: מנא תקל פרסין (*Mene, Tekel, Parsin*)</note>. These things indeed represented this to **Nebuchadnezzar**: *God has numbered your kingdom and finished it. It has been weighed in the balance and found wanting. Your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians.*

### THIRD BOOK. LXXVII

Either, therefore, a single word dispersed through its letters produces many words, or many words reduced through certain letters are gathered into one; hence from many, one, and from one, many. This is shown to be by no means strange by the frequent use of two monosyllables, as they say Virgil <note>original: "Maronem"; referring to Publius Vergilius Maro</note> wrote in his poems: *"Yes and No are the monosyllables known to all and used frequently; if these are taken away, there is nothing left of human affairs that speech can revolve."* Therefore, almost all conversations of all men signify "Yes" and "No." For this reason, in this art, who would wish to doubt that a whole word can be noted by a single letter, and an extended speech by a single word? And likewise, vice versa, a chosen and intended word can be noted by a single speech.

From this arises a certain hidden and wonderful **technology of letters** <note>original: "epistolarum technologia"; referring here to steganography or cryptography</note>, which I have often imitated in grave dangers and in the greatest crises of affairs. I wrote in the German language through a letter what I desired to be understood by a Latin man in Tuscany or Etruria; and in the reverse manner, I wrote in Latin what I wanted a German man, unskilled in Latinity, to know. I would wish you to receive this, whatever it may be, with a grateful mind and store it away diligently in your deepest senses, for it is no small matter.

In practice, if we work correctly, letters of this kind come to us in four ways:

For they either take [letters] from the beginning of a word to signify something else, as in the beginning of **Genesis** <term>The first book of the Bible</term>: *The sixth day. And the heavens were finished* <note>original Hebrew: יום הששי ויכלו השמים (*Yom HaShishi Vayechulu HaShamayim*); the first letters of these four words (Y-H-W-H) form the Name of God</note>; behold the **Tetragrammaton** <note>The sacred four-letter name of God</note>. <margin>H</margin> Or [they take letters] from the end of any word, as in **Psalm 1**: *Not so the wicked* <note>original Hebrew: לא כן הרשעים (*Lo khen ha-reshaim*)</note>, which when transposed make **Amen** <note>original Hebrew: אמן</note>. For he wished this to be understood: *Not so the wicked*, because they will not say "Amen," and for that reason they will be sent into **Gehenna** <term>A place of punishment or purgatory in Jewish tradition</term>.

Or there are those letters which offer themselves individually, any one of them contained within a whole word, as in **Psalm 3**: *Many rise up against me.* Who are these "many"? The **Kabbalists** <term>Students of Jewish mysticism</term> answer: **RBM** <note>original Hebrew: רבם (*Rabbim*), meaning "many"</note> are the **Romans**, **Babylonians**, **Ionians** <note>Greeks</note>, and **Medes**.

Or finally, they are not intended relative to the constitution of other words, but any one of them takes a meaning according to its own property. For example, when mention is made of two worlds, the letter **Yod** <note>The smallest letter of the Hebrew alphabet, י</note> signifies the world to come, and the letter **He** <note>The letter ה</note> signifies the present world, namely this world. **Genesis 2**: *These are the generations of the heaven and of the earth when they were created* <note>original Hebrew: בהבראם (*be-hibare'am*)</note>, that is, *in He He created them* <note>A wordplay on the Hebrew word "when they were created," which contains the letter He</note>.

Undoubtedly, this final consideration of letters pertains to the substance of the character itself, but by no means to an accidental relation as the previous three did, which related to something else. For in this designation they now signify—either according to grammatical instruction—the things themselves offered in the first position; or numbers ordered by the discipline of arithmetic; or certain reasons applied to the words of **Our Masters** <note>The Rabbinic sages</note>; or finally, every creature proceeding from the **First Cause** <term>God</term>, and reducible again into the First Cause. Concerning the primitive position of letters, they show it thus: that **Aleph** <note>The first letter, א</note> is a path or instruction. Whence **Job 33**: *I will teach* <note>original: "docebo"; related to the root of Aleph</note>—that is, I will instruct—you in wisdom. **Beth** <note>The second letter, ב</note>, a house; **Psalm 23**: *I will dwell in the house of the Lord.* **Gimel** <note>The third letter, ג</note>, retribution or reward; **Psalm 116**: [The Lord has dealt bountifully with me].

<meta>This page continues the technical breakdown of the Hebrew alphabet as used in Kabbalistic study. The previous page discussed the art of using single letters to represent whole words or phrases (Notarikon); here, the speaker Simon begins to define the "grammatical" meaning of each Hebrew letter and its symbolic significance, bridging linguistics with mystical philosophy.</meta>

### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART
## BOOK THREE. LXXXVII

<note>original: "Daleth"</note> Because the Lord has rewarded you. **Daleth**, a door, an entrance, or a gate, Genesis 19: *And they were close by, so that they might break the door.* **He**, behold, Genesis 47: *Behold the seeds for you.* **Vau**, a twisted hook, Exodus 26: *Whose capitals shall be of gold.* **Sdain** <note>Also known as Zayin</note>, weapons, 4 Kings 22: *And they washed the weapons according to the word of the Lord.* **Heth**, terror, Job 7: *You will terrify me through dreams.* **Teth**, a turning away <note>original: "declinatio"</note>, through the transposition of the letter Teth, Proverbs 4: *Do not turn away to the right or to the left.* **Iod**, a confession of praise, Genesis 49: *Your brothers shall praise you.* **Caph**, the palm of the hand, Ecclesiastes 4: *Better is a palm full of rest.* **Lamed**, doctrine or teaching, Psalm 143: *Teach me to do your will.* **Mem**, waters, Isaiah 55: *All who are thirsty, come to the waters.* **Nun**, sonship <note>original: "filiatio"</note>, Isaiah 14: *Son and grandson.* **Samech**, an addition or placing upon, Deuteronomy 34: *Because Moses imposed (that is, added) his hands upon him.* **Ain**, an eye, Exodus 21: *An eye for an eye.* **Pe**, a mouth, Exodus 4: *Who placed a mouth in man?* **Tzade**, sides, Exodus 25: *Six branches shall come out of its sides.* **Kuph**, a revolution or circuit, Exodus 34: *At the return of the season of the year* <note>original: "Redeunte anni tepore"</note>, that is, the circuit of the year. **Res**, poverty, Proverbs 10: *The fear of the poor is their poverty.* Others, however, interpret it as "inheritance." **Sin**, a tooth, Job 4: *And the teeth of the young lions are worn down.* **Thau**, a sign or mark, Ezekiel 9: *Mark a Thau upon the foreheads of the men.* 

This is the grammatical exposition of the letters: how people are accustomed to impose names on things, whether original or derivative. Nothing, I believe, is foreign to higher speculation, if anyone should emerge as a student of figurative speech. 

Then **Philolaus** said: "It seems to me that we must become 'elementary schoolers'—old men who once again have need of the schoolmaster's rod <note>original: "ferula"</note>. For in the meantime, with much study, we have been reduced back to the alphabet." 

And **Marranus** added: "Certainly we are growing young again; this is that Pythagorean rebirth <note>original: "palingenesia"</note> of yours, Philolaus." 

To which **Simon** replied: "Do not reject it; it is truly a great matter and worthy of philosophers—if you believe your own Plato—and not at all ridiculous, as it seemed to Socrates in the *Cratylus*, to know the letters. For we have nothing better than that, he says, by which we may judge concerning the truth of the first names: <note>original Greek: "ἐπειδὴ δὲ συλλαβαῖς τε καὶ γράμμασιν ἡ μίμησις τυγχάνει οὖσα τῆς οὐσίας, ὀρθότατόν ἐστι διελέσθαι τὰ στοιχεῖα πρῶτον"</note> *'since the imitation of essence happens to be through syllables and letters, it is most correct to distinguish the elements first.'* 

From this I think they are called **elements** <note>original: "elementa"</note> as if they were **matter-ments** <note>original: "hylementa," a creative etymology combining the Latin 'elementa' with the Greek 'hyle' (matter)</note>, that is, material things, from which the greatest things are made out of the smallest. As Hesiod says: *'If you add a little to a little, and put it all together, the heap will finally become large.'* 

"Proceed, Simon," said Philolaus, "for you speak everything truly; let us have joked with your permission in this conversation." 

Then he continued: "I shall pass to the numbers of the discipline of arithmetic, which are designated by the Hebrew letters. For there is no other language in the space of the whole world whose letters show any given numbers so perfectly. Nevertheless, the recent Greeks have attempted..."

### BOOK THREE
## PAGE LXXVIII

The Jews imitated [the Greeks], so that they might similarly represent numbers using their alphabet. But it was necessary to insert two additional figures for themselves, for both the number sixty <note>This likely refers to the "stigma" for 6 and "koppa" for 90 in the Greek system, which the author is comparing to Hebrew needs</note> as well as the ninetieth, which figures are not literally part of the alphabetical order. For these two signs, **ϛ** <note>the Greek stigma, used for 6</note> and **ϟ** <note>the Greek koppa, used for 90</note>, are the inventions of modern men led by a desire for imitation, for which matter we cite the books of Homer as evidence. Certainly, the Romans explain few numbers by letters; on which matter you once read **Priscian of Caesarea** <note>A famous 6th-century Latin grammarian</note> writing to Symmachus regarding numbers, weights, and measures.

Therefore, let us create four grades of numbers: the first is of digits, the second of tens, the third of hundreds, and the fourth of thousands. The first grade is noted by the characters of the alphabet from **Aleph** to **Teth**. There are nine signs, referring individually to nine numbers, such as **א ב ג ד ה ו ז ח ט**, that is: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine.

The second order, of tens, also contains nine characters of the alphabet: **י כ ל מ נ ס ע פ צ**, that is: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety.

The third grade, of hundreds, similarly has nine characters: **ק ר ש ת ך ם ן ף ץ** <note>This includes the five "final" forms of letters used at the ends of words</note>, that is: one hundred, two hundred, three hundred, four hundred, five hundred, six hundred, seven hundred, eight hundred, nine hundred.

The fourth grade is of thousands, in which one must return to the characters of the earlier numbers, although they ought to be larger in stature, so that it is called a "Great Aleph," like a wide Aleph, and it is pronounced with a **pathach** <note>a Hebrew vowel mark indicating an 'a' sound</note> according to the Italian 'a'. Thus a Great Beth signifies two thousand. From there up to nine thousand, and finally a Great Iod for ten thousand; in this order, some are accustomed to mark the characters with points <note>original: "apicibus"</note> instead of size. Afterward, they do not use characters, but words: **רבו רבותים** <note>original Hebrew: *ribbu, ribbotayim*</note>, that is: a thousand thousands, twice a thousand thousands, and so on.

This way of using the alphabet for numbers has been most greatly embraced by the **Kabbalists**, who say that two thousand years of a "Beginning" preceded before this world was made. This is because before **Bereshit** <note>original: "בראשית", the first word of Genesis meaning "In the beginning"</note>, the beginning of the scripture, he places a Great Beth, saying: **בראשית**. In this way, our sages explain that passage in Proverbs 8: *The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his ways, before he made anything from then.* <note>Proverbs 8:22, referring to Divine Wisdom</note> Truly, whatever exceeds thousands is held in the place of the infinite. For the end of numbers in the sacred texts are thousands, as when David wished to show the infinity of value in Psalm 119, he said: *The law of your mouth is better to me than thousands of gold and silver,* <note>Psalm 119:72</note> that is, without number.

Now let us briefly review the third species of the substance of letters, which refers to certain intentions of our Teachers. For example, **Aleph-Beth** signifies to them "prudence" <note>original: "alephi-binah," a pun on the names of the first two letters</note>, and **Gimel-Daleth** signifies the "rewarding of the poor" <note>original: "gemol dallim"</note>, and **Mem**—that is, **Meamar**—clearly signifies "open speech" and "hidden speech," and so with the others which we will recite a little further below, though these are more frequent in **Talmudic** usage. The fourth species of these letters—

# ON THE KABBALISTIC ART
## PAGE LII

[The study of these letters] consists in all established and created things. It is especially useful to students of Kabbalah <note>The Jewish mystical tradition that explores the relationship between the eternal God and the finite universe</note> so that they may more easily lead creatures back to the Creator, which is indeed the greatest and unique aim of that discipline. I will therefore place each of the letters in its own order, so that you may know each element individually, and thus I begin. From **Aleph** to **Iod** <note>The first ten letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note> the orders or choirs of angels are signified, which the philosophers call "separated intelligences" and "noble, incorporeal, and insensible forms." These proceed and derive from the power of God, who has no form, nor image, nor likeness. For he said in Isaiah 40: "To whom have you likened me, that I should be equaled?" And a little before: "To whom then have you likened God? Or what image will you provide for him?" Furthermore, that dwelling place is named **The World of Angels** <note>original: עולם המלאכים, Olam ha-Malakhim</note>, that is, the angelic age or the angelic world.

Then, from the letter **Caph** to the letter **Zade**, the orders of the heavens are designated. These are granted power by God the Creator and are governed by the influence of the angels; this is called **The World of Orbs** <note>original: עולם הגלגלים, Olam ha-Galgalim</note>, that is, the age of the spheres or celestial bodies.

Furthermore, from **Zade** to **Thau**, there come the four elements with their forms, and all mixed things together, both living and non-living, which depend on the power of God. From Him, the power to be and to live flows into them, as it says in Isaiah: "Creating the heavens and stretching them out, establishing the earth and the things that spring from it, giving breath to the people who are upon it, and spirit to those who tread upon it, or walk in it." These things are directed by the influences of the angels and the spheres, and the whole of it is called **The World of Elements** <note>original: עולם היסודות, Olam ha-Yesodot</note>, that is, the age of elements. Within it is Man, who is called **The Small World** <note>original: עולם הקטן, Olam ha-Katan</note>, which the Greeks call a <term>microcosm</term> <note>original: μικρόκοσμος</note>, that is, a lesser world, or more rightly, a world in miniature. For in man himself, the properties of all creatures, both the highest and the lowest, shine forth.

Perhaps we shall recall these things to memory more usefully if we demonstrate of which things the individual letters are said to be symbols. This is a truly pleasant matter, celebrated by the most ancient authors, lest there be some in the future who mock this art as if it were thin and meager.

Therefore, **Aleph** is the mark of the highest and most exalted things, which subsist by the first outflow of divine goodness; for example, the angels, who are called **Holy Living Creatures** <note>original: חיות הקדש, Hayyoth ha-Kodesh</note>, that is, animals of the sanctuary, or rather, lives that exist without a medium directly beneath God. These angels, by the power of God, purify, illuminate, and perfect those immediately below them, which in common speech is called their "influence."

**Beth**, the second letter, signifies the second grade of angels from God himself, who are called **Wheels** <note>original: אופנים, Ophanim</note>, that is, forms or wheels. In the second place, they are derived from the power of God through the prior intelligence, and they themselves also flow from God into lower things. The wise have also said at the same time that **Beth** is the mark of Wisdom.

**Gimel** represents, among the higher essences, the angels who are called **Mighty Ones** <note>original: אראלים, Aralim</note>, that is, angels [who are] great and strong... <note>catchword: gni fortes</note>
