# BOOK THREE

...great, strong, and robust beings who descend in the third order from the goodness of the divine majesty. They are illuminated by the power of God through the second intelligence, and they likewise flow into those below them. **Daleth** <note>The fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet</note> is the symbol of the fourth emanation among the heavenly beings who are called the **Hasmallim** <note>original: חשמלים; often translated as "glowing ones" or "amber-colored ones," representing a high rank of angelic beings</note>. In the power of God, they receive influence through the medium of the third intelligence, and by that same power, they flow into those below them.

The letter **He** designates the superior beings of the fifth emanation from God himself, which are the **Seraphim** <note>original: שרפים; literally "the burning ones," known for their intense love and zeal for the divine</note>. They receive the influence of God’s power through the medium of the fourth intelligence and, by that same power, flow into those below.

**Vau** <note>Also known as Waw</note> denotes the essence of the superior beings of the sixth emanation, who are called the **Mallachim** <note>original: מלאכים; meaning "messengers" or "angels"</note>. They receive influence from the power of God through the medium of the fifth intelligence and flow into those below by that same power.

**Zain** is the seal of the blessed superior spirits of the seventh emanation, who are named **Elohim** <note>original: אלהים; here used as a title for a specific rank of angels often associated with divine justice or power</note>, that is, "gods." They receive influence from the power of God through the angels of the sixth order and flow into those below by that same power.

**Heth** is the sign of the superior beings of the eighth emanation; these are the angels called **Bne Elohim** <note>original: בני אלהים; "the sons of God"</note>, that is, the sons of the Gods. They are filled by the power of the Almighty <note>original: El</note> through the angels of the seventh order and flow into those below by that same divine power.

**Teth** is the mark of the angels of the ninth emanation, who are called **Cherubim** <note>original: כרובים</note>. They receive influence from the power of God through the medium of the intelligence of the eighth order and flow into those below by that same power.

**Iod**, the tenth letter, signifies the essence of the intelligences of the tenth emanation. They are called the **Issim** <note>original: אשים; literally "men" or "individuals," referring here to "souls of fire" or noble spirits</note>, the noble ones and the patricians. They are the lowest of all the hierarchies and are illustrated by the power of God through the ninth choir. By that same power, they flow into the children of men, providing them with knowledge, the science of things, and a wonderful industriousness. Hence, those who are endowed with such a faculty are called "sons of the **Issim**," that is, men of noble intelligence. Of these, it is said in Psalm 49: "Both the earth-born and the sons of men," which is properly read as: "both the sons of the common people and the sons of the patricians," as if one were saying, "both the rustic and the noble." 

We ourselves take this name from this order of intelligences. For there is in us an "active intellect," the highest part of the soul which **Aristotle** calls the *nous* <note>original: νοῦν; Greek for "mind" or "intellect"</note>, that is, the mind, which alone comes to us from the outside. From this proceed prophetic visions and all things great and holy. It is called the **Active Intellect** <note>original: שכל הפועl, Sekel Ha-Poel</note>, by which the angelic world is bounded.

There follows **Caph**. This letter designates the **First Mover** <note>The outermost sphere of the universe in traditional cosmology</note> directly from the Almighty God <note>original: El Sadai</note> as the first cause, though moved communicatively through the spirit of rational life, which is the angel **Metattron** <note>Metatron is often described in mystical texts as the "Prince of the Countenance" or the highest of angels</note>. He is called the "active intellect of the sensible world," providing a path for all inferior things through the penetration of forms; therefore, he flows by divine power into everything that is movable.

**Final Caph** <note>The form of the letter used at the end of a word</note> signifies the circuit of the **fixed stars**, which is called the eighth sphere in relation to us. However, in relation to the superior realms, it is the second orb, divided into the twelve signs of the zodiac, which we...

...we call **Mazzaloth** <note>original: מזלות; refers to the constellations of the Zodiac or the fixed stars</note>, and it is influenced by the power of God through the medium of the intelligence of **Caph** itself, and similarly it flows into lower things. **Lamed** is the sign of the first sphere of the planets, and they are called **Leketh** <note>original: לכת; derived from the Hebrew root for 'walking' or 'moving'</note> as if they were wayfarers, whom the Latins call 'wanderers' <note>original: errones</note>, following the Greeks, who for that reason assert they are **planets** <note>original: πλανήτας; literally 'wanderers'</note>. And it is called the seventh orb <note>counting inward from the fixed stars</note> attributed to Saturn, whom we call **Shabbatai** <note>original: שבתאי; related to 'Shabbat' or rest</note>; it flows and is influenced.

Open **Mem** <note>the standard form of the letter used at the beginning or middle of words</note> marks the sphere of Jupiter, because it is named **Tzedek** <note>original: צדק; meaning 'Justice' or 'Righteousness'</note> by us, and is influenced by the power of God through the medium of superior intelligence, and by that same power flows into lower things. Closed **Mem** <note>the final form of the letter, ם</note> is the symbol of the sphere of Mars, whom we call **Maadim** <note>original: מאדים; meaning 'the Red One'</note>, the fifth orb; it is influenced by the power of God the Creator through the angel immediately above it, and by that same power flows into lower things.

**Nun** signifies the greater light, which is called **Shemesh** <note>original: שמש</note>, that is, the Sun, and its sphere is called the orb of **Chamah** <note>original: חמה; meaning 'Heat'</note>; it is influenced by God through the medium of the sixth intelligence, by which it also flows into lower things. Final **Nun** indicates the sphere of Venus, which is called **Noga** <note>original: נגה; meaning 'Brilliance' or 'Bright'</note> by us, and it consists of the power of God and flows by means of the seventh intelligence.

**Samech** is the symbol of the chancellor <note>a title for Mercury as the celestial scribe or messenger</note>, who is called **Cochab** <note>original: כוכב; literally 'Star'</note>, and in Latin *Mercurius* [Mercury]; he is influenced by the power of God from those above, and by that same power flows into lower things.

**Ain** is the mark of the sphere of the Moon, which is called **Iareah** <note>original: ירח</note> by us, and it appears as the left eye of the world. It is the last of the orbs among the star-bearers, and because of its whiteness, it is sometimes named **Lebanah** <note>original: לבנה; meaning 'the White One'</note>. All these things we entrust to the faculty of astrology.

**Pe** signifies the intellectual soul, both individual and universal, and it is directed by the separate intelligences into which it is poured by God, both in the spheres and in the stars, and in all superior and inferior living beings of the spheres and elements. Final **Phe** denotes the animal spirits, which are directed by the superior intelligences by the power and command of God.

**Zade** symbolizes matter—both that of the heavens, which is intelligible, and that of the elements, which is sensible—and of all mixed things. They are directed, moreover, by divine power through separate intelligences and through their own forms. Final **Zade** shows the forms of the elements, which are fire, air, water, and earth. And they are governed by divine power through the angels, who are called **Issim** <note>original: אישים; literally 'Men,' the tenth and lowest rank of angels in the hierarchy, who govern the physical world and human souls</note>, and by the power of the heavens, and by the power of primary matter, which is the source and origin of all elements.

**Kuph** is the symbol of inanimate things and minerals, and of those things which are called 'elemented' <note>complex bodies composed of the four elements</note> and mixed. They are directed, however, by divine power through the celestial spheres and separate intelligences, which are called **Issim** <note>original: אישים</note>. And they flow into lower things in the region of the four elements.

**Res** signifies all vegetation, fruits, and crops, and the things born of the earth; they are influenced by the power of God from the celestial bodies and separate intelligences by the name of **Issim** <note>original: אישים</note>, and likewise by the complexions of the elements, **Sin**...

# BOOK THREE

...creatures. **Sin** <note>the letter ש</note> designates all sentient things, including the reptiles of the earth and those that walk, as well as the fish of the waters and the birds of the air together, and whatever irrational things possess vital motion. These are ruled by the power of God through the celestial bodies and the Intelligences, which we call **Issim** <note>original: אישים; literally "Men" or "Individuals," referring to the tenth and final rank of angels in the hierarchy of Maimonides, who bridge the gap between the divine and the physical world</note>, and through the tempering of the elements.

**Thau** <note>the letter ת</note> is the symbol of man and human nature, which is the perfection and the goal of all created things. It is directed by God through the temperaments and qualities of the elements according to the influences of the heavens and through the specific duties of the separate Intelligences, the **Issim**, who are of an angelic condition. And just as they are the end and fulfillment in the world of angels, so man is the end and perfection of creatures in the world of elements—or rather, in the world of the universe. For he was established from two worlds, as it is written: *The Lord God formed man from the dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life.* <note>Genesis 2:7</note>.

These matters are treated more fully by our elders, whose descendants show a most burning love for the sacred letters; they strove to provide a reason for even the smallest details. For example, concerning **Aleph** <note>the letter א</note>, it is written in the book *Ha-Bahir* <note>original: הבהיר; "The Book of Brightness," one of the earliest and most important works of Kabbalah</note>, that is, *On Radiance*, where Rabbi Amorai sat and disputed why **Aleph** is placed at the head of the alphabet. The answer given is that it existed before all things, even before the Law <note>the Torah</note>. Menahem Recanati <note>a famous 14th-century Italian Kabbalistic commentator</note> mentions this regarding Rabbi Rahumai (the author of that book) in the first section of Genesis.

Furthermore, why does **Beth** <note>the letter ב</note> follow immediately? Certainly because it was the beginning of the Law <note>The first word of the Bible, "Bereshit," begins with the letter Beth</note>. And why is **Gimel** <note>the letter ג</note> not called *Gidel*, since in the sacred scriptures *GL* <note>the root for joy or revelation</note> is placed before it and *GML* <note>the root for weaning or recompense</note> follows it? This is seen in Genesis 21, where it is written: *And the child grew [va-yigdal] and was weaned [va-yigamal].* Wise men certainly did not disdain to investigate such matters.

However, there are also a number of those who, for the sake of brevity, passed over the explanations of some things and wrote only what simply pertained to the matter, since they always endeavored to hasten toward more sublime things with all diligence and study. Such was Rabbi Jacob Cohen in the book titled *Perush Ha-Shem Ha-Kadosh* <note>original: פירוש השם הקדוש; "Explanation of the Holy Name"</note>. Regarding the alphabet, he speaks briefly as follows:

**Aleph** is Air; **Beth** is Life; **Gimel** is Peace; **Daleth** is Wisdom; **He** is Sight; **Vau** is Hearing; **Zain** is Smell; **Heth** is Speech; **Teth** is Feeding <note>original: לעיטה; often referring to the gluttonous eating or "infusion" of food</note>; **Iod** is Rest <note>original: משכב; literally "the bed" or "lying down"</note>; **Caph** is Wealth; **Lamed** is Work; **Mem** is Water; **Nun** is Motion; **Samech** is Spirit; **Ain** is Laughter; **Pe** is Seed; **Zade** is Thought; **Kuph** is Sleep; **Resh** is Grace; **Sin** is Fire; **Thau** is Dominion.

It is as if he had enumerated them with these words: Air, life, peace, wisdom, sight, hearing, smell, speech, feeding, rest, wealth, business, waters, movement, spirit, laughter, seed, meditation, sleep, grace, fire, power.

These and other similar things which you have heard from the monuments of the fathers, I have gathered as briefly as I could, so that I might offer you at least some taste of this literary profession. Indeed, the distinguished author Rabbi Akiba <note>a foundational figure in Rabbinic Judaism and traditional author of mystical texts like the "Alphabet of Rabbi Akiba"</note> wrote of these things with great care, and many have followed his lead.

-># ON THE ART OF KABBALAH<-

...from our own people, the most learned men, whom we deem worthy of much honor. For they have said that many senses lie hidden in the exposition of the alphabet. And Rabbi **Abraham Ibn Ezra** <note>a celebrated 12th-century Spanish-Jewish scholar and polymath</note> says of this in the book entitled *Sodot HaTorah* (סודות התורה), that is, *On the Mystery of the Law*: "And the truth is that it is good for the intelligent man that he should learn from wisdom" <note>original: והאמת כי טוב הוא למשכיל שילמד מאת החכמה</note>. He says this not so that we should labor in the literary art for the whole time of our life, as if we were to be tormented day and night in the volumes of **Rabbi Judah** <note>Judah ben David Hayyuj, the "father of Hebrew grammar"</note>, who is said to be the first grammarian among the Hebrews; or in those twenty books that **Marinus** <note>Jonah ibn Janah, a famous medieval Hebrew grammarian and lexicographer</note> composed on literary instruction; or those twenty-two that **Samuel Nagid** <note>Samuel ha-Nagid, a 11th-century statesman and scholar in Granada</note> published on the same subject. Thus far speaks Abraham Ibn Ezra, nor did that most prudent man and most skilled in letters feel this way in vain, for we were born for greater and higher things.

I have just spoken of the four considerations that pertain to the substance of the letter; now, in my opinion, I must conclude that which we began a while ago regarding the accidental relationship of letters, which is called **Notarikon** (נוטריקון) <note>a system of shorthand or acrostics where letters of a word stand for whole sentences, or vice versa</note>. <margin>o</margin> In this part, we consider which letter signifies which word. It has three species. For when it takes a certain sign from the beginning of a word, and (as is usually done) marks it with points at the top, it is called **Rashiti Teivot** (ראשיתי תיבות), that is, "the head of words" <note>acrostics using initial letters</note>, and it is customarily written thus: **ה׳**. Likewise, when it is taken from the term and end of any proposed word, it is then called **Sofi Teivot** (סופי תיבות), that is, "the end of words" <note>acrostics using the final letters</note>, which they have been accustomed to figure in this way: **ת׳**. But if, however, individual marks are derived from the individual letters of any word, we then call that by the general name **Notarikon**. <margin>p</margin> 

To these things **Philolaus** <note>one of the fictional scholars in this dialogue</note> said: "O our Simon, how secret and hidden these things are to outsiders." 

Then **Simon** <note>the Jewish sage acting as the teacher in Reuchlin's work</note> said: "I will show you perhaps much more occult things in this third part of Kabbalah, which is called **Temurah** (תמורה) <note>a method of substituting one letter for another according to a specific cipher or system</note>, where a mutual substitution of letter for letter occurs, and it happens as many times as the alphabets are permuted. They are permuted according to the number of the letters, twenty-two times, because we read twenty-two Hebrew letters; and by always joining any two letters, it will be permitted to take one for the other. That combination is called **Tziruf** (צירוף). For example, if from these six letters of the Latin alphabet—**a b c d e f**—I should continually join them two by two, so that under the first yoke are **a b**, under the second **c d**, and under the third **e f**, and I wished to urge someone skilled in this art through a letter that, as he is about to petition the prince, he should fall before his feet. Thus I write: **dbcf**, which he will understand as **Cade** <note>Latin for "fall"; the substitution follows the pairs: c becomes d, a becomes b, d becomes c, e becomes f</note>; and so it is with others. This whole workmanship comes from the alphabetic revolution, so that one letter succeeds another in turn, combined in its own yoke: namely, **a** for **b** and **b** for **a**, similarly **c** for **d** and **d** for **c**, and likewise **e** for **f** and **f** for **e**. This proceeds more easily in Hebrew, with nothing standing in the way, because the sounds which the Latins call vowels are not in...

This mixture of the twenty-two elements <note>meaning the 22 letters of the Hebrew alphabet</note> is by no means to be understood in a crude or unlearned way, for all things are spirit. Thus it is written in the book *Yetzirah*: "**And with that spirit God engraved twenty-two letters: three mothers, seven doubles, and twelve simples, and each of them is spirit.**" These things were handed down to us so that we might contemplate them spiritually with great joy, not for speaking against them or mocking them. Rather, the mysteries of the Scriptures are to be embraced with pious faith. For by believing in the letters, we more easily contemplate higher things, and we trust that hidden things can be found in the letters—as if they were the word of God in the midst of darkness, who said to Moses: "**Behold, I come to you in a thick cloud, that the people may hear when I speak with you**" <note>Exodus 19:9</note>, and indeed

### ON THE KABBALISTIC ART

...devotion and confidence, as in Psalm 70: *Let them exult and be glad in you* <note>original: כב (Kaf-Beth), meaning twenty-two</note>—that is, in the twenty-two [letters]—those who seek you. For you should know that the twenty-two letters are the foundations of the world and of the Law, as is treated at length in the second book of the *Nut Orchard* <note>original: *Horti nucis*; this refers to the *Ginat Egoz*, a foundational Kabbalistic text by Joseph Gikatilla</note>, which you have either read or are currently reading.

Then **Philolaus** said: "Certainly, I have never read nor even seen such books, even though I have searched with no small effort until now to find where they might be hidden."

And **Marranus** said: "I do not know why the Jews are so stingy with books of that kind, such that they do not even share them freely with friends, or sell them at any price."

Then **Simon** said: "It is a statute for us that the secrets of the Law are not to be given to strangers, but only to a *wise counselor* <note>original: ליודע חכם (*le-yodea chakham*)</note>. And not just to any domestic counselor, nor just to any wise man, but specifically to a 'wise counselor' who is neither an outsider nor unlearned. I beg you not to take this poorly. For often, because of the danger hanging over us during our long dispersion, the concerned assembly of our fathers prudently decreed: *By that law, he himself should flee from that into which he later fell* <note>original: ברת שהוא ברח ממח שנגל בו באחרונה; Simon is explaining that secrecy was a survival mechanism during the Jewish Diaspora</note>. Our authority for this is **Moses the Egyptian** <note>Maimonides (1135–1204), the preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher</note>, who enumerates the causes and recites the events in the sixty-first chapter of the first book of the *Guide for the Perplexed* <note>original: *libri primi perplexorum*, referring to Maimonides' *Moreh Nevukhim*</note>. But I hope you will take these and other matters of our nation in good part; therefore, leaving that dispute aside, I will proceed with the third part of the Kabbalistic art."

"You have heard about the two hundred and forty-two combinations of letters and the two hundred and thirty-one permutations of pairings, besides the commonly used alphabet; however, they are also accustomed to connecting every two letters of that alphabet in their own order for mutual exchange. This is a matter commonly seen as trivial and perhaps, at first glance, held in contempt by the unskilled, but it is one that should be greatly exalted by men. As we read in Psalm 12: *Vileness is exalted among the sons of men* <note>original: כרם זלות לבני אדם (*karem zulut livnei adam*)</note>. Regarding this, **Rabbi Solomon** <note>Rashi (1040–1105), the famous biblical commentator</note> cites what is said by the Psalmist: *The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner*."

"I pray you, do not consider it carelessly, for it was not written in vain as *Karem* <note>original: כרם; 'vineyard' or 'exaltation'</note>; for according to <term>Gematria</term> <note>the Kabbalistic practice of calculating the numerical value of Hebrew letters to find hidden meanings</note>, it signifies two hundred and forty-two. For that is the total number of combinations described above, and from those, you should venerate the two hundred and thirty-one variations with fitting honor. For everything that exists and everything that is spoken arises from them. Concerning those 'Gates,' as they call them, our father **Abraham** said in the book *Yetzirah* <note>The *Sefer Yetzirah* (Book of Formation)</note>: *And it is found that every word and every creature proceeds from the One* <note>original: ונמצא כל הדבור וכל היצור יוצא מאחד</note>. Indeed, with the help of these letters, we can easily arrange ourselves for our own salvation, since we are to be led back through the consideration of all created things to a knowledge of the one Creator—as far as human strength allows—which is our salvation and eternal life. This is situated in God, through His Name, and back into God again. He is Himself His own four-letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton (YHWH)</note>, forever blessed, which the Psalmist showed when he said: *And they shall know that You are [Your] Name...*"

LXXXI

### BOOK THREE

...your Tetragrammaton <note>The "Tetragrammaton" refers to the sacred four-letter name of God, YHWH.</note> alone is supreme for you over all the earth. For this reason, this name alone is called the *Semhamaphoros* <note>original: *Semhamaphoros*, a Latinization of the Hebrew *Shem Ha-Mephorash*, meaning the "Explicit" or "Distinct" Name</note>, that is, the explanatory name of the essence of God. The demonstration of this is taken from the first part of this art. There is another name of God that succeeds it, which is written with twelve letters, and the reason for that will be received from the second part. There is, furthermore, another name which is most conveniently discussed in this third part of the Kabbalah.

<margin>S</margin>
The Name of forty-two characters. This does not mean that a single pronunciation of one name consists of forty-two letters. For it is known to any intelligent person, as Moses Maimonides <note>A preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher (1135–1204)</note> teaches, that a single name written with so many letters can be found nowhere. Rather, these are several names, complex among themselves and within themselves, gathered from many letters. These lead the Kabbalist through certain hidden ratios to the true knowledge of God’s Tetragrammaton:

<margin>T</margin>
יהוה יהוה <note>The Tetragrammaton repeated: YHWH YHWH</note>, which similarly, through arithmetic <note>The author refers to Gematria, the practice of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters to find deeper meanings.</note>, signifies forty-two. Forty-two characters of this kind, joined together through such names, are called "one name" because they ultimately signify only one thing: just as, conversely, other composite and collective names are often many words signifying a single thing. It could therefore happen in the present circumstances that the ratio by which our intellect is led into God could not be explained except through many letters and words. This is not surprising, since ingenious craftsmen are accustomed to track a spring through many different streams. Thus, from the abyss of His own fountain, God made all things flow out, and flow back again into an infinite whirlpool.

*To bring forth a thing in a word, and a word in a thing, until all things are established in the spring of the flame, and the flame in the word, in a spring that has no searching and no number, for the light that is hidden in the increase of darkness, concealed within the total of forty-two letters.* <note>original Hebrew: להוציא דבר במאמר... This is a mystical quote describing the emanation of the universe from a divine source.</note>

These are the words of the most contemplative teacher, Hamai <note>Rabbi Hamai Gaon, a figure to whom several early Kabbalistic works are attributed.</note>, in the *Book of Contemplation* <note>original: *Sefer Ha-Iyun*</note>, to which he usefully cites the *Book of the Fountain of Wisdom* <note>original: *Sefer Ma'ayan Ha-Chokhmah*</note>, although a man of such integrity would not have lacked for testimony. Now I will try to see if I am able to interpret these things into English, at least so that the meaning suffers no loss.

<margin>V</margin>
"In order to produce," he says, "a thing in a word, and a word in a thing, until he restored all things into the fountain of radiance, and the radiance into the word, as if into a fountain of which there is neither limit nor number, toward the inaccessible light hidden by the addition of darkness in the universe of forty-two letters." Thus far Hamai. Moreover, the most excellent of the sages (whose memory is a blessing) call this name—so venerable and to be worshipped, designated by forty-two letters—*Holy and Sanctified* <note>original Hebrew: קדוש ומקודש (*Kadosh u-Mekudash*)</note>. Therefore, it was hidden from the unrefined and the unworthy through the mixing of alphabetic revolutions, and was revealed through Jeremiah <note>The prophet Jeremiah</note> only to the saints who lead a contemplative life, by means of alphabetic combinations; he was often known to read...

LXXX ON THE KABBALISTIC ART

...he used to do in the *Book of Formation* <note>original: *libro Ietzira* (*Sefer Yetzirah*), one of the foundational texts of Jewish mysticism</note>, as is found written in the *Book of Trust* <note>original: בספר בטחון (*Sefer Bitachon*)</note>, that is, in the Book of Hope, whose author is Rabbi Judah, who composed it. And since Jeremiah <note>Hieremias refers to the prophet Jeremiah, who in medieval legend was associated with mystical practices</note> turned the pages of the *Book of Formation* much and often by night and by day, a Heavenly Voice <note>original: בת קול (*Bat Kol*, literally "daughter of a voice")</note> is said to have come to him, which commanded him to labor over that same volume for three years. Therefore, after the end of three years, when the joining and study of the characters finally pleased him so that he might work with them, soon a new man <note>A "new man" refers to a Golem, a creature brought to life through the mystical application of Hebrew letters</note> was created for him and his companions, and on his forehead was written "The Lord God is Truth" <note>original: יהוה אלהים אמת (*YHWH Elohim Emeth*)</note>, that is, the Tetragrammaton God is True. Then that recently created man, sensing the writing on his forehead, did not delay any further, but suddenly with a swift hand moved and removed the first letter in "Truth" <note>original: אמת (*Emeth*)</note>, which is the letter *Aleph*. Thus, the remainder stayed with these words:

<margin>ד</margin>
"The Lord God is Dead" <note>original: יהוה אלהים מת (*YHWH Elohim Meth*). By removing the letter Aleph from *Emeth* (Truth), only *Meth* (Dead) remains.</note>, that is, the Tetragrammaton God is dead. Because of this matter, Jeremiah, struck with indignation, tore his garments and said to him: "Why do you take away the *Aleph* from *Truth*?" He responded: "Because everywhere people have failed in faithfulness to the Creator, who created you in his own image and likeness." Jeremiah said: "How then shall we apprehend him?"

<margin>ה</margin>
He responded: "Write the alphabets backwards in this scattered dust according to the understanding of your hearts" <note>original Hebrew: כתבו האלפאביתות למפרע באותו העפר הנזרק כבינת לבבכם</note>, that is, write the alphabets in reverse into this dispersed dust, according to the insights of your hearts. And they did so. And that man became dust and ashes in their sight, and so he disappeared. Wherefore Jeremiah asserted that he had then received from God Himself the virtues and powers of the alphabets and of elementary permutations, for he had previously known the arrangement of the combination from the *Book of Creation*. From there, this alphabetic Kabbalah—that is, "reception"—passed down to posterity, through which the greatest secrets of divine things are opened. For when we have led that great name, which is to be extolled with the greatest strength, through all combinations of letters from the last to the first, then the divine knowledge of Him will liberally show itself to us, and will offer its powers to our will and mercifully submit to it—if He finds us worthy, and endowed and fortified with purity of mind, sincerity of faith, firmness of hope, and the ardor of love.

<margin>ו</margin>
For our fathers—as Rabbi Tarphon, Rabbi Moses the Egyptian <note>Moses Maimonides (1135–1204), a famous Jewish philosopher and physician</note>, and Rabbi Hamai, and others have written—did not wish, according to the precepts of our Masters, to show that name to any mortal, unless he was exceedingly worthy. For they said thus: that it is not handed down except to a humble man, and to one who stands in the middle of his days, not to one who is angry, nor to a drunkard, nor to one defiled by wicked morals, but to a man of peace, and one who speaks sweetly with creatures, and who guards it with purity; for such a person is beloved above and desired among us below, and the fear of him falls upon all creatures.

# BOOK THREE. LXXXIII

...then any word into two small phrases, each of which contains three letters according to the idiom of the Hebrew language. Therefore, having performed the arithmetical multiplication by saying six times seven, there will be forty-two letters—that is, the entire collection of the letters of that Name—which I submit to the inspection of your eyes in this inscription <note>original: "charagmate," a Greek-derived term for a mark, character, or inscribed sign</note> as follows: 

-> שגת במא שגתתכץ מיתחצב ימיבתה צגהפז תגזמה נאצפפש <-

Indeed, while I am counting how many letters are in this verse, immediately any one of the seven disyllabic parts of the phrase is born for me. For each and every phrase of this most precious Name is known to consist of six characters, though only in Hebrew, and not in any other language. For in Latin <note>original: "Latine," referring to the Roman/Latin alphabet used in the translation</note> more letters will be needed, such as Sagathbama, Sagaththechaz, Miathazab, Iemibatha, Zethagaphaz, Thegazama, Naazpapas, which are found in the volumes of the ancients even unto this day as foreign and unknown to the Roman tongue <note>original: "Romano sermone"</note>, but they are not to be despised simply because they are harsh and barbaric <note>In a Renaissance context, "barbaric" refers to words that do not follow Greek or Latin grammatical rules, often used to describe mystical or foreign terms</note>.

<margin>X</margin>
For let no one use eyes so blurry in the sight of sacred things that he condemns what is hidden; let no one indulge his ears in such delights when hearing divine matters that he only venerates, praises, and follows those things which are pleasant to the senses, beautiful to the eyes, soft to the touch, and charming in their pronunciation. Rather, let him grasp spiritual things more than physical ones, constant things more than fleeting ones, and true things more than those that are merely painted over. Indeed, harsh and rough things often precede the presence of God. Remember what happened to the prophet Elijah <note>original: "Eliae prophetae"</note> when he was hiding in the caves and in the hollows on Horeb, the mountain of God; was it not said to him thus: "Behold, the Four-Lettered Lord <note>original: "Tetragrammatus"</note> passes by, and a great and strong wind overturning mountains and breaking and crushing rocks before the Four-Lettered Name <note>original: "Tetragrammaton"</note>, but the Lord was not in the wind; and after the wind a commotion <note>original: "commotio," here referring to an earthquake</note>, and the Lord was not in the commotion; and after the commotion a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire; and after the fire a thin, small voice, and in that voice the Glory of the Four-Lettered Name spoke to him," which is called Glory <note>original: כבוד (*Kavod*)</note>. So you, after the desert,

<margin>Y</margin>
horrid and thorny—after the mountain and the rocks, after the wind and the earthquake, after the fire, after the voice—having dismissed the multitude of secular preoccupations in the very vestibule of the caves and hollows, you shall hear the Glory of God speaking to you: "What are you doing here?" Proceed further, as is explained in the Third Book of Kings, chapter 19 <note>In modern Bibles, this is 1 Kings 19</note>. Therefore, we must not stand still here, but we must return with the prophet Elijah <note>original: "Eliha," a variant spelling of Elijah</note> to our own path through the desert—that is, through these bristling revolutions of barbaric connections and tangled briars—into the path of the sacred and canonical Scripture, a path truly ours, which is the truth of the utterances of God, so that we may anoint the king in Syria, who is called the Messiah <note>original: "Messiha"</note> from his anointing. For a while, we shall walk through the combinations <note>original: "coniugationes"</note> of the twenty-two alphabets, until with watchful solicitude we reach the supreme and first alphabet...

# ON THE CABALISTIC ART

<meta>catchword: & earth,</meta>

...and has been reached with unwearied diligence. For we must skillfully run through each combination until the voice of God lies open, and the open text of the most sacred scriptures offers itself to us. That very voice of God abundantly rains down its power and value upon all alphabets from the first to the last—that is, the twenty-second—so that combinations which are not considered to have a primary meaning provide a somewhat greater efficacy than names with a primary meaning, just as a ray of the sun burns more strongly than the sun itself from which it flowed. <note>Reuchlin argues that the "raw" power of divine letter combinations is more potent than the literal meaning of the words, comparing it to the focused intensity of a magnifying glass.</note> From this comes that saying of the Count of Mirandola <note>Giovanni Pico della Mirandola (1463–1494), a key figure in the development of "Christian Kabbalah."</note> in his *Conclusions*, where he says: "Any voice has power in Magic insofar as it is formed by the voice of God." Therefore, the power, operation, vigor, efficacy, completion, and perfection of the present Name of forty-two letters depends upon the voice of God. We intend to hunt for this through all the connections and nets of every alphabet, until we are able to find the seven names comprised of forty-two letters anywhere in the sacred scripture. For example: if one searches from the first and twentieth alphabet for seven similar words, which could be symbols for any verse of divine scripture, let them be set down for me safely, just as they were mentioned above. Likewise from the twentieth, and even further from the nineteenth, and in the same way running through all of them in succession down to the first, which received its name from its beginning (just like the others) so that it is called *Albath* <note>original: אלבת. This refers to a specific system of Hebrew letter substitution where the first letter (Aleph) is paired with the eleventh (Lamed), the second (Beth) with the twelfth (Mem), and so on.</note>. From its combination, let us borrow this example:

-> ABG DHV ZChT IKL MNS EPZ QRSh TRL TZLK QLD VTzTz LRV QNN BQB QTzTz <-

which is also a divine Name of forty-two letters received from the first alphabet of the *Book of Creation* <note>original: "libri Ietzira," referring to the Sefer Yetzirah, one of the foundational texts of Jewish mysticism</note> in a permuted form. For our father Abraham placed only permuted and transposed letters in that *Book of Creation*, since he did not doubt that the direct order of the common alphabet was known to everyone. However, they are also accustomed to combine this in a similar way, saying *Ab Gad* <note>original: אב גד, another permutation system</note>, as Rabbi Hamai <note>A legendary figure often associated with early Kabbalistic texts like the Sefer Ha-Iyyun.</note> taught in that *Book of Speculation* <note>original: "de Speculatione," referring to the Sefer Ha-Iyyun</note>. He also describes a name of forty-two letters produced from that same combination of his, like this:

-> ABGTShT AQBTzBV TNTShVT NTNHBSh VBQPHV BTPVTSh VShHTA <-

which likewise, like the others, symbolically signifies the Blessed God according to His property. For just as the Ineffable Four-Letter Name <note>The Tetragrammaton (YHWH)</note> denotes God as He is above all being, and *Ehieh* <note>Hebrew for "I Am"</note> represents God as He is in all being, and *Adonai* <note>Hebrew for "Lord"</note> represents God as the ruler of all, and *Sadai* <note>Shaddai, Hebrew for "Almighty"</note> as needing nothing, so in a similar way, any name of forty-two letters—whether it be received from transposed or direct combinations—designates God insofar as He is the creator of heaven and earth, and of all things visible and invisible. For this reason, those twenty-three divine names (each of which is drawn with forty-two figures) are said to be derived, according to the orders of the twenty-three alphabets, from the first two verses of sacred scripture: *In the beginning God created heaven and earth,*

...and the earth, for the earth was void and empty. <note>original: "et terram, terra autem erat inanis & uacua." There are also other Cabalists <term>Cabalists (mystics practicing Kabbalah)</term> of a more sublime speculation, who transcend creation and created things and persist only in the emanation of the Divinity. This emanation they receive and record under a faithful silence for men most worthy and devoted to God, through the holy name of twelve characters and the name of forty-two letters. This is written **in the book "The Epistle of Secrets"** <note>original: "בספר אגרת הסודות" (Be-sefer Iggeret ha-Sodot). ->**Father is God, Son is God, Holy Spirit is God, three in one, and one in three**<-
<note>original Hebrew: "אב אלהים בן אלהים רוח הקדש אלהים שלושה באחד אחד בשלושה" (Ab Elohim, Ben Elohim, Ruach ha-Kodesh Elohim, sheloshah be-echad, echad be-sheloshah).</note>

Oh, how great is this height, how great the depth, which is apprehended by faith alone! Then Philolaus said: "Indeed, Simon, what great thanks must be given to you, who shows us all things so clearly and brightly—if indeed anything in this art can be clear, and is not rather for the most part hidden in wrappings, and seen to 'flee to the willows.'" <note>An allusion to Virgil's *Eclogues* (3.65), suggesting a truth that reveals itself only to hide again.</note> And Marranus said: "Be silent, I beg you, Philolaus. Then Simon replied: "I have completed the entire art and taught it, unless there are things you think remain in detail regarding certain names of God, and of angels and powers, and consecrated seals, by whose force and power many have promised they would perform many things which might seem admirable to the common people."

And Marranus said: "Perhaps forgetfulness has seized you, for you were also going to speak of the name of twelve letters, although you asserted it was the subject of the second part, <margin>C</margin> which has already passed." Then Simon said: "There is little I might explain about that, except that after the name Tetragrammaton became cheapened everywhere by the frequent and common use of wicked men—having previously been treated with such care, solicitude, reverence, and such prudent moderation—it was handed down only to suitable and chosen priests every seven years, so that they might learn to bless the people in the sanctuary through it. Then, to preserve the majesty of this name, the priests were forbidden to use it in prayer, and its pronunciation was permitted only to the high priests once a year on the days of fasting and atonement. Therefore, in its place, they substituted for the others the name of twelve letters, which was somewhat more sacred than the name *Adonai* <term>Adonai (the Hebrew word for "Lord")</term>, and yet fell far short of the ineffable Tetragrammaton..."

That is to say: "Therefore the priests extend their hands, saying, the Holy One, blessed be He, stands behind us, just as it is written: 'Behold, He stands behind our wall, observing from the windows from between the fingers of the priests.'" I hold this written thus on the parchment of an ancient codex, although certain printed paper volumes lack these words. Truly, our people believe most firmly and in no way doubt that a blessing expressed in this form is the cause of as much prosperity as it would have been if the name Tetragrammaton—which they now pronounce as *Adonai* <note>meaning "Lord"</note>—had remained in those prayers. For whatever other symbols, notes, sacraments, or signs of divine things are found, they surely take their origin from this very source.

LXXXV

### BOOK THREE

<margin>E</margin> Concerning this very point, He is called <term>Elohim Kadoshim</term> <note>original: "Elohim Kadosim," meaning "Holy Gods."</note>, that is, the "Holy Gods" in the final chapter of Joshua, and <term>Elohim Chayyim</term> <note>original: "Elohim Haiim," meaning "Living Gods."</note>, that is, the "Living Gods" in the fifth chapter of Deuteronomy. And in the first chapter of Malachi, He speaks of Himself thus: <term>And if I am Lords, where is my fear?</term> <note>original: "ואם אדונים אני איה מוראי" (Ve-im adonim ani aye morai).</note> In this passage, God refers to Himself in the plural as "Lords." Therefore, according to His inner essence He is one, but according to His emanations <note>original: "egressiones," referring to the divine outgoings or manifestations.</note> He is many, for He said: "Let us make man in our image and likeness." It was not simply a custom of the Holy Language that those <margin>H</margin> established in the highest majesty should speak of themselves in the plural, as Rabbi Saadia writes in the book <term>Beliefs and Opinions</term> <note>original: "אמונות" (Emunot). Saadia Gaon (882–942) was a prominent Jewish philosopher who argued that the plural form was a "plural of majesty."</note>. This is a weak argument, because immediately afterward He speaks in the singular, saying: "I will make him a helper like unto himself." The Cabalists do not unwillingly admit this unity and this plurality in divine matters for various reasons, whence they assert that the first three Cabalistic numerations <note>original: "numerationes," referring to the Sephirot or divine emanations.</note>—<term>Keter, Hokhmah, and Binah</term> <note>original: "כתר חכמה בינה" (Crown, Wisdom, and Understanding).</note>—are the one crown of the Supreme King, as Rabbi Assë writes in the book <term>Tagin</term> <note>original: "תגי" (Tagi), a mystical work concerning the decorative crowns on Hebrew letters.</note>, a unique work on unions or collections. You see by this example that we use all parts of the Cabala indiscriminately: namely, the universal transposition of letters, syllables, and words; then numerical calculation <note>term: Gematria</note>; then the notation of capital letters <note>term: Notarikon</note>; and the literal exchange of letters, along with the individual types which I revealed in my previous discourse. For instance, we transpose the four-letter name <note>The Tetragrammaton, YHVH.</note> so that it becomes <term>Va and Ia</term>, from which arises <term>Havayah</term> <note>original: "הויה," meaning "Being" or "Essence."</note>, which is the first of all things, from which all true and good beings exist. Hence, <term>Ehieh Adonai</term> <note>original: "Ehieh Adonai," meaning "I Will Be [the] Lord."</note> signifies numerically the same as <term>Elohim</term>, the sum of which is eighty-six. Just as <term>Mah</term> <note>original: "מה," a mystical name meaning "What."</note> is a marker of <term>Elohim</term> itself if it is expanded as <term>Aleph, Lamed, He, Mem</term> <note>original: "אלף למד הי מם," spelling out the letters of Elohim.</note>, that is, eighty-six. And <term>Yah</term> <note>original: "יה," a shorter form of the divine name.</note>, the Tetragrammaton name, because it is twenty-six; but if it is <margin>F</margin> expanded as <term>Yod, He, Vav, He</term> <note>original: "יוד הי ויו הי," the full spelling of the letters Y-H-V-H.</note>, it makes one hundred twelve and designates <term>Tetragrammaton Elohim</term>, that is, the "Lord God." Concerning this, it is first written: "These are the generations of the heaven and the earth when they were created, in the day that the Lord God [Tetragrammaton Elohim] made the earth and the heaven." Moreover, the beginning of the Tetragrammaton name is <term>Yah</term>. And the middle of <term>Elohim</term> is <term>Yah</term>, and the end of <term>Ehieh</term> is <term>Yah</term>. All of this is the perfection of <term>Being</term> <note>original: "יהיה" (Yehiyeh).</note>, which signifies "Himself" and "to be divine." Hence it is a worn-out daily usage to say that "being" itself is something divine, necessary, and incorruptible. For everything that exists, when it exists, is <margin>G</margin> necessary by virtue of this, nor can it then happen not to be. Therefore, the power of that Essence led into operation through the Word of God, who said <term>Let there be</term> <note>original: "יהיה" (Yehiye), but likely referring to "יהי" (Yehi) from Genesis.</note>; by which word all the Ideas and the most absolute intellectual virtues were created in one sum, through the fact that He commanded: "Let there be light," and soon light was made. This universality was followed by the nature of the angels assigned to ministries, when He said: <term>And it was so</term> <note>original: "ויהי כן" (Vayehi khen).</note>, which designates the Prince and Great Priest, who is named Michael, a bright proof of the angelic...

### ON THE CABALISTIC ART

<sig>q</sig>
<meta>catchword: virtues</meta>

<margin>a</margin> ...of the condition which is constituted from unity and the number one hundred. Whence they believe that on the first day, the Ideas were produced outside the first cause, being the most absolute forms in both their being and their operation. However, on the second day, they say the angels were created. For on the first day, the scripture did not say, **"And it was so,"** <note>original: "ויהי כן" (Vayehi ken)</note> that is, "it was made thus"; but rather on the second day, when the firmament of heaven was made. According to **Rabbi Eliezer** <note>Rabbi Eliezer ben Hurcanus, a 1st-century sage often cited in mystical literature.</note>, it was created from the light of His garment. For God was clothed in ten garments when <margin>H</margin> He created the world, as the Cabalists say, and from the light of His last garment He took and created the heavens—not indeed the sensible ones, but those invisible and intellectual **spirits and spiritual entities** <note>original: "רוחות ורוחניות" (Ruchot u-ruchaniyot)</note>. Regarding these, the Psalmist says: *The heavens declare the glory of God*, where the word for **Heavens** is not written as *Shamayim* <note>original: "שמים," referring to the physical, circular orbs.</note>, which refers to the orbs; this was memorably noted by **Rabbi Ama** in the *Book of Secrets* regarding Psalm 19. Instead, it is written as **The Heavens** <note>original: "השמים" (Ha-Shamayim)</note>, to which the article *ha* is added. As we read in the summary argument of Genesis: *In the beginning God created the Heavens* <note>original: "Hasamaiim"</note>, that is, those distinguished heavens, those world-renowned heavens, those admirable heavens, never seen nor to be seen by mortal eyes.

For the other heavens, which are written without the article *ha*, are indeed the firmament, yet they are still called by the name of "heaven." For this reason it is written: *And God called the firmament "Heavens."* And this is called the firmament of the invisible heaven itself, which is termed the **Heaven of Heavens**. Whence it follows: *Let there be lights in the firmament of heaven.* Truly, that extension in the manner of a skin, as if inscribed with letters by the luminaries and stars, is called **Rakia** <note>original: "רקיע" (Rakia), usually translated as "expanse" or "firmament."</note> because of its local expansion, which we call "firmament" because of its stability.

For the invisible heaven had no need for luminaries, since it is spiritually illustrious through itself and mentally illuminated by the First Cause. Therefore, they are named the "separate intelligences," of whom the **Author of Causes** <note>A reference to the *Liber de Causis*, an influential Neoplatonic work attributed to Aristotle in the Middle Ages but actually based on Proclus.</note> says: *Every intelligence is full of forms.* While such an intelligence understands, it is said to "hear" and to "speak," which is why Moses says: *Give ear, O heavens, to what I speak.* And David says: *The heavens declare the glory of God.* And God says in Hosea: *I will hear the heavens, and they shall hear the earth.* From this source descends the prophetic light which is called the **illuminating vision** <note>original: "אספקלריא המאירה" (Aspaklaria ha-me'irah), literally an "illuminating mirror" or "lens." In Jewish mysticism, this represents the highest level of prophecy.</note>, which belonged to Moses. For the vision of other prophets was a **non-illuminating vision** <note>original: "אספקלריא שאינה מאירה" (Aspaklaria she-einah me'irah)</note>, and that is called "earth." Some mention of these things was made in our first discourse. Indeed, I believe I am right to trust what our sages said: *The appearance of Moses was like the appearance of the sun, and the appearance of Joshua was like the <margin>D</margin> appearance of the moon.*

Therefore, in the creation of sensible things, God uses this symbol of the intelligible world: **"And it was so"** <note>original: "ויהי כן" (Vayehi ken). In Cabalistic gematria, the numerical value of "Vayehi Ken" is 101, which is the same as the name of the angel Michael.</note>. This designates the ministry of angels <margin>I</margin> created together with natural things under the common name of **Michael**, which serves as a title for the angelic species. Through that phrase **"And it was so,"** repeated in the works of the following five days, it is symbolically signified according to the first part of the Cabalistic art through the equality of numbers. By this we are taught that all angels are of the same species; furthermore, individual bodies, whether celestial or earthly, have their own specific governors.

Reuchlin explains that angels and spiritual "Ideas" were created from divine light and that the prophetic clarity of Moses far exceeded that of later prophets.</summary>

LXXXVI

### BOOK THREE

...of virtues and perfect operations, both those that are rational—such as the heavens, the stars, and humans—and those that are irrational, such as the beasts and the elements. Indeed, it is first proven by the **Peripatetic philosophers** <note>Followers of Aristotle, who taught while walking in the "peripatos" or covered walkway of the Lyceum.</note> that any spherical heaven, besides its own essential form, has an **assisting intelligence** <note>original: "assistentem intelligentiam"</note> that moves its orb. This is called an **angel**, for it is sent for this office, and, understanding and willing, it fulfills the commands of the Creator. It acts as a middle power between God and Nature, through which operations occur in things that their own nature either would not do, or would not do in such a way. Some say these operations come from a **hidden property** <term>occulta proprietas: a quality of a substance that cannot be explained by the four elements, like magnetism</term>, and others say it is because they are such. For although the motion of the heavens and stars is naturally circular, to be moved from the East to the West, or vice versa, is not a matter of nature, but of **will**. 

For an angel has free will, whereas nature is constrained only by a certain instinct, whereby it always acts in the same way; however, angels do not always move the orbs in the same way. Thus it happens that the changes in these lower things do not always occur in the same manner. For the angelic condition exercises the greatest force and power over corporeal things; therefore, the **Active Intellect** <note>In medieval philosophy, the "Intellectus Agens" is the power that allows the human mind to grasp universal truths.</note> from which forms flow is named an "angel," as **Rabbi Moses Maimonides** <note>A preeminent medieval Jewish philosopher (1135–1204).</note> testifies. It is called **The Prince of the World** <note>original: "שרו של עולם" (Sar Ha-Olam)</note>, as our sages have said, and it is named **Metatron**. By him, indeed, all individual human, animal, and natural virtues are governed, which are likewise called "angels." Their multitude is infinite to us, but to the Creator, it is certain, delimited, and finite. **Bereshit Rabbah** <note>An ancient collection of Jewish interpretations on the Book of Genesis.</note> mentions this matter, where it is read that the Creator daily creates a host of angels, whom others call "forms," because they are formal substances with which the entire sphere of things that can be born and perish is filled without number. 

In no other way did your **Hesiod** <note>An early Greek poet, often cited alongside Homer.</note> also receive this, for in *Works and Days* he says: **"For thrice ten thousand are the immortals of Jove upon the nourishing earth, guardians of mortal men, who watch over justice and cruel deeds, clothed in air, wandering everywhere over the earth."** <note>original Greek: "τρὶς γὰρ μύριοί εἰσιν ἐπὶ χθονὶ πουλυβοτείρῃ ἀθάνατοι ζηνός..."</note> <margin>כ</margin> In the likeness of these, they name two powers of the will in man as two angels: **The Good Inclination and the Evil Inclination** <note>original: "יצר טוב ויצר רע" (Yetzer tov ve-yetzer ra)</note>, as is read in the **Midrash Tanchuma**, which **Rabbi Ashi** <note>A famous Babylonian rabbi and primary redactor of the Talmud.</note> cites in his collection. Moreover, the Latins call such Hesiodic guardians who assist the body "spirits." Whichever of them is destined for the care of lower business is called **Mammona** or **Mammon**, whom the Greeks call a **daemon** or **demon**, though not in a bad sense. Certainly, a "daemon" is one thing, and a "demonium" <note>An "imp" or lesser demon.</note> is another, which we think is a diminishing of divinity; therefore, it is excluded from divine things as a diminutive term, although I clearly confess that to Homer and the most ancient writers... <margin>i</margin>

...that there was another use for that word <note>The word being discussed is "daemon" or spirit.</note>, when many people spoke in praise and veneration of the **guiding spirit** <note>original: "daemonio." Thus far Tedacus Levi. > **For from the earth unto the firmament there is no empty place, but all is full of multitudes of them—some pure, some masters of grace and mercy; and there are below many foul, harmful, and accusing creatures, and they all stand and fly in the air. And from the earth unto the firmament there is no empty place, for it is entirely filled with species—some for peace, some for war, some for good, some for evil, some for life, and some for death. And all this is in the lower dwelling in which we exist.** <note>original Hebrew: כי מן הארץ ועד הרקיע אין שם מקום פנוי אלא הכל מלא המונים... וכל זה במדור התחתון שאנו בו</note>

This is what **Joseph of Castile** <note>Joseph Gikatilla (1248–1305), a Spanish Kabbalist whose work bridged philosophy and mysticism.</note> says.

<margin>K</margin>

# BOOK THREE #

<margin>L</margin>
They consider themselves to have experienced many things, and they do not doubt their ability to attract good spirits by soothing them, and to repel malignant ones by opposing them with contrary passions, being duly supported by sacred and divine names and characters. They command that a man who is to be exposed to future dangers should receive a very thin parchment, which is called **virgin [parchment]** <note>original: "membranam... uirginea". This refers to parchment made from the skin of a stillborn or very young animal, symbolized as "pure" and "unblemished" for ritual use.</note> because it is sincere, clean, and immaculate, so that it may foreshadow the purity of the practitioner. Then, they should transcribe these characters: **Tzamarkad** <note>original Hebrew: צמראבד. This is a mystical name formed from the final letters of the first five verses of Genesis.</note>. However, on the outer, rougher part of the leaf, they also write these signs: **V-V-V-V** <note>original Hebrew: וווו</note>. By this binding <term>ligatura: a charm or amulet meant to "bind" spiritual forces</term>, they instruct the person who most firmly hopes in God, the Creator of the universe, to fear no machinations of wicked men. They reveal the mystery in this way: these are symbols of the first five verses of **Genesis**, using both the beginnings and the endings of the words according to the second part of the **cabalistic art** <note>This refers to the practice of Gematria or Notarikon, where new names are formed from the initials or terminal letters of scripture.</note>. Once, **Costa Ben Luca** <note>Qusta ibn Luqa (820–912), a Syrian Christian physician and translator known for his works on physical charms and medicine.</note> wrote about **physical ligatures**—though these were not truly physical matters—which he claimed were proven by experience. He said that if the pinky finger of an aborted fetus is hung around a woman’s neck, she will not conceive as long as it stays there. But now, if such things are believed, they ask: should anyone think that the words by which the **Almighty Creator** made heaven and earth have no power when bound [as a charm]? Indeed, men of my school believe much in the great master **Rabbi Asse** <note>Rabbi Ashi (c. 352–427), a primary codifier of the Babylonian Talmud.</note>, who wrote in the **Book of Unity** <note>original: "Sefer ha-Yichud".</note> that one who wishes to seek and obtain his desires should turn to the clemency and mercies of God by using these characters: **Anakatam Pastam Paspasim Dionsim** <note>original Hebrew: אנקתם פסתם פספסים דיו נסים. This is the 22-letter name of God, often associated with the Priestly Blessing.</note>. These are found to be worthy memorials of Holy Scripture, of which there are many others that fill almost all the books of the Cabalists. Others also study how to manufacture illustrious **seals** <note>original: "sigilla".</note> from the divine letters, which are proven by long use to be effective against human illnesses and other troubles. For example, there is that which **Rabbi Hama** <note>Likely referring to Rabbi Hamai Gaon, to whom the "Sefer ha-Iyun" (Book of Speculation) is traditionally attributed.</note> composed in the **Book of Speculation** from four names that are not magical, but solemn and common sacred names—or rather, he received them as already composed by the fathers: **The Lord, My Lord, Y-Y-Y, I Shall Be** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה אדני ייי אהיה. These are the names YHWH, Adonai, a triple-Yod representation of God, and Ehyeh.</note>. According to the Cabala, "I Shall Be" <note>original Hebrew: אהיה (Ehyeh)</note> is the same as **El** <note>God</note>. Therefore, the practitioners of this science take the first character of the first name, the first of the second, the first of the third, and the first of the fourth, and the first seal is formed: **Y-A-Y-Y** <note>original: יאיי</note>. Then they work in the same way with the second letters of the four most sacred names, and **H-D-Y-Y** <note>original: הדייי</note> arises. They fashion the third seal by joining each of the third letters, and **V-N-Y-Y** <note>original: ונייי</note> is born. Finally, in the same manner, they couple the last letters, and the fourth seal emerges, which is **H-Y-H-H** <note>original: הייה</note>. The intention of these four seals is **The Lord is our God, the Lord is one** <note>original Hebrew: יהוה אלהינו יהוה אחד. This is the Shema, the central declaration of Jewish faith.</note>, and they say this should be the inscription of the four seals joined together. Finally, on the back of the parchment, they depict **ARARITA** <note>original Hebrew: אראריתא</note>, which they interpret thus: **One, the beginning of His unity, the beginning of His singularity, His exchange, One** <note>original Hebrew: אחד ראש אחד ותו ראש אחד ייחודו תמורתו. This is a famous kabbalistic acronym (Notarikon) where each letter of ARARITA stands for a word in this sentence.</note>. And this "exchange" is understood...

### ON THE CABALISTIC ART ###

...literary [art] according to the third part of the **Cabala**. They stand, therefore, with their seals and inscriptions before God, most high in their devoted minds; and whatever blessing they might request from those eighteen blessings, or those contained in other righteous prayers, they hope to obtain without fail. They trust that they can frequently break every fate even when it is imminent from heaven, or mitigate **Adrastia** <note>original: "Adrastiam". In Greek mythology, Adrastia was a goddess of inevitable fate or divine retribution. Here, Reuchlin uses it to mean the inescapable power of divine laws.</note>—that is, the inevitable power of divine laws—through the prayers of sacred words. For they believe that a well-initiated **Cabalist** is able to perform any number of wonderful things, not only with characters and figures, but even with words and incantations. Some of your own thinkers confess that this is possible. For **Plotinus**, in the second book of *On the Doubts of the Soul*, chapter thirty-five, enumerates four things in which a marvelous power resides: namely, the occult qualities of species, figures, harmonies, and vows. **Porphyry** and **Iamblichus** <note>Plotinus, Porphyry, and Iamblichus were major Neoplatonist philosophers who explored the relationship between the material world and the divine.</note> also say that through God specifically, and through the good angels, we have command over the lowest spirits. Nor is there any race of men in the whole circuit of the earth who more easily agree with this opinion than (as the report goes) the more divine **Christians**, who cast out demons by names and figures, and lay hands upon the sick and they recover, and they heal deadly things and perform similar miracles. But, to speak the truth as they assert it, they attribute all these things to faith rather than anything else, although they also think that a certain power is inherent in prayers. For they say and believe that the prayer of faith shall save the sick; nor do the fit Cabalists feel differently, for they likewise affirm that miraculous prayers depend on God alone and on the faith of the man. Therefore, they pronounce those to be liars and fools who grant such great force and power of miracles to the figure alone, to the writing alone, to the lines alone, or to the mere voices born of broken air, as **Rabbi Moses the Egyptian** <note>Rabbi Moses Maimonides (1138–1204), the preeminent Jewish philosopher, often referred to as Rambam.</note> testifies in the first book of the *Guide for the Perplexed*, chapter seventy-two.

<margin>M</margin>
To these things, **Philolaus** says: "Not only the Cabalists of the Hebrews, but even the most excellent of the Greeks have attributed much to the signs and seals of faith." For **Antiochus**, surnamed **Soter** <note>Antiochus I Soter (c. 324–261 BC), a king of the Seleucid Empire.</note>, when he was on an expedition against the Galatians—brave men fortified by an innumerable gathering of soldiers—and was about to engage in a most difficult battle, at a time when (as **Lucian** writes of him) <note>original Greek: "πάνο πονηρὰς εἶχε τὰς ἐλπίδας" (pano poneras eiche tas elpidas)</note> **he had very dismal hopes**, he saw in a dream at night **Alexander** standing by him. Alexander ordered that before the fight he should proclaim to his soldiers a certain sign of health as a military token, through which he promised that victory would fall to him. It was of the kind that was marked on their clothing, as the same man of Samosata <note>Lucian of Samosata, the Greek satirist.</note> noted in *A Slip of the Tongue in Greeting*: <note>original Greek: "ἔταξαν δὲ ζύγγον δι' ἀλλήλων τὸ πεντάγραμμον" (etaxan de zyngon di' allelon to pentagrammon)</note> **they arranged the pentagram as a sign among themselves**—that is, the triple triangle formed of five lines. Moreover, once that sign was raised, Antiochus obtained a wonderful victory against the Galatians. I myself have indeed often seen that symbol of the pentagon struck on the silver coinage of Antiochus; when resolved into lines, it shows the word <note>original Greek: "ὑγίεια" (hygieia)</note> **Health**. Will it not...

### BOOK THREE ###

"It will be to the point," Marranus said, "that which once appeared from above to the great Constantine—that sign of God, as they then called the cross—at the very hour of noon in the sight of the whole army, inscribed with Latin letters thus: *In this, conquer*. <note>original: "In hoc uince". This refers to Constantine the Great’s famous vision before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge in 312 AD.</note> And indeed, Constantine did conquer by that same sign; he was then elected and hailed as Emperor by the applause of the Roman people and was surnamed the most invincible of all Emperors. Therefore, how much power seals and signs have possessed will be attested by the greatest men: **Maccabeus** for the Jews, **Antiochus** for the Greeks, and **Constantine** for the Romans. <margin><image-desc>A Christogram or Chi-Rho symbol (☧) with a horizontal crossbar through the stem of the Rho, creating a cross-like appearance.</image-desc></margin>

<margin>N</margin> Nor does it escape you, Simon, what you said a little earlier regarding the **Christians**. For in this age, there is no race more admirable in the crafting of signs, characters, and words than those who, by the figure of the cross and the name of **JESUS**, stay the seas, calm the winds, and repel lightning. Furthermore, there is nothing stronger than that character and image of the cross, and nothing more health-bringing in times of danger. To speak freely, this is for no other reason than because they stand as the symbol of the true Savior, just as that name, the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>The four-letter, unpronounceable Hebrew name of God, YHWH.</note>, is the symbol of God for you.

What the **Cabalists** are able to do with the ineffable name along with the seals and characters you recently demonstrated, the faithful Christians can do in a much more powerful way through the pronounceable name of **JESUS** with its own sign of the cross. They believe that they pronounce the name **Tetragrammaton** far more correctly in the name <note>original: יהושע (Yehoshua/Jesus)</note> of the true Messiah. To support this, they cite what your own people wrote in the **Midrash Tehillim**: <note>The "Midrash Tehillim" is a traditional Jewish commentary on the Book of Psalms.</note>

*Rabbi Joshua son of Levi said, in the name of Rabbi Phineas son of Jair: For what reason does Israel pray in this world and is not answered? Because they do not know the <term>Shem HaMephorash</term>,* <note>original: "Semhamaphores," meaning the Explicit or Distinct Name of God.</note> *that is, the name **Tetragrammaton**.*

<margin>Q</margin> Thus it is written there. Then Simon said: "Perhaps you are right, but why use more words? Certainly, the wiser **Cabalists** wish to relate this figure of the cross to the wood of the bronze serpent erected in the desert, <note>A reference to Numbers 21:9, where Moses set a bronze serpent on a pole to heal the Israelites.</note> though they do so very silently and in secret. They do this through <term>Gematria</term>, <note>A system of Hebrew numerology where letters represent numbers.</note> which is the equality of numbers. For the characters of these two words, <note>original: צלם (Tzelem), meaning "image" or "sign."</note>—that is, the cross—and <note>original: עץ (Etz), meaning "wood" or "tree."</note>—that is, the wood—both symbolize the number **one hundred and sixty**. <note>In Hebrew numerology, both Tzelem (90+30+40) and Etz (70+90) equal 160, creating a mystical link between the "wood" of the serpent's pole and the "image" of the cross.</note> Therefore, a transition is easily made from one to the other: from the cross to the wood, and from the wood to the cross.

But I press my finger to my lip to stay silent. The shortage of time constrains us, my best friends, so that I have said less than I intended; yet I am frustrated, and I begrudge losing that growing joy I felt from the ornament and dignity of your speech. Now, in such deep night when it is time to sleep, I shall stop. You have not disputed with me like common, trivial, or thin-voiced Sophists, nor with a gladiator’s battle of words or a contention of opinions, but with an accurate and sharp method of speaking, using thoughts suited and adapted to the matter at hand. I could wish that longer spans of days were granted to us. For no one [has spoken better] regarding the **Cabalistic** art..."

It can hardly be said enough in a short time, for these matters are so great, so deep, so innumerable, and so full of distinctions, that anyone eager and studious of this cause must strive with the greatest powers of the mind. One must look around not only at the diligence with which it must be learned, but also the danger with which it must be moderated and practiced. For since this science concerns spiritual things and is itself spiritual, and since a man cannot easily pass judgment on spirits—even one to whom the power of judging between angels and demons has been granted through careful discernment or the use of a precise rule—it is certainly not without great fear, and only after one's character has been purified, that this faculty and exercise should be properly undertaken. This is to ensure that we do not suffer the fate of the prophet Balaam <note>Balaam was a non-Israelite prophet in the Book of Numbers who was warned by an angel not to curse the Israelites; he is often cited as an example of one who possesses spiritual power but lacks the moral standing to use it rightly.</note>, nor imitate the mother of the living <note>Eve, often referred to as "the mother of all living" (Genesis 3:20).</note>, nor follow darkness under the guise of light. Fear for yourselves from those spirits cast down by lightning <note>A reference to fallen angels, such as Lucifer, cast out of heaven.</note> and our most savage enemies; and believe me, they carry their own banners among us mortals, just as the angels do. In the army of God, there are four standard-bearers: <term>Michael, Gabriel, Uriel, Raphael <note>original: מיכאל גבריאל אוריאל רפאל</note></term>, who are like the four elements, or the four spiritual positions, or the four spiritual numberings <note>Reuchlin likely refers to the Sefirot, the ten emanations in Kabbalah, here grouped or associated with the cardinal directions.</note>, just as the sons of Israel set out under four banners in the second chapter of the Book of Numbers. Furthermore, there swarm great troops of demons and fugitive legions of the underworld, all of whom have their portion in the scapegoat <note>The "goat for Azazel" mentioned in Leviticus 16, which was sent into the wilderness bearing the sins of the community.</note>. For this whole philosophy of ours...

For I know they do not cease daily to test your pious ears with whispers, sometimes through hired intermediaries, sometimes through letters—such as the one I recently read, sent to you from Cologne <note>original: *Agrippina Colonia*</note> on the 14th of the Kalends of October, in which the title also lies about the author alongside the false accusation. ### ON THE CABALISTIC ART ###

<margin><image-desc>A magical sigil or character consisting of a central cross with diagonal lines and small crossbars or circles at the terminals.</image-desc></margin> No one can say enough in a short moment, for these matters are so great, so deep, so numerous, and so full of distinctions, that anyone eager and studious of this cause must strive with the greatest powers of their mind. Unless one’s character is first purified, this faculty and exercise cannot be properly pursued, lest we suffer the fate of Balaam the prophet <note>Balaam was a non-Israelite prophet in the Book of Numbers who was rebuked by his own donkey and later died in battle against Israel</note>, lest we imitate the mother of the living <note>original: *viventium matrem*—a reference to Eve and the Fall in Eden</note>, or lest we follow darkness under the guise of light. The Cabalists zealously approve of this, saying:
